nodes.statement:
An abelian category has abelian Hom groups, finite direct sums, kernels and
cokernels, and the usual normality and factorization axioms.  A complex is a
sequence $d^{i}:A^{i}\to A^{i+1}$ with $d^{i+1}d^i=0$; its cohomology is
$\ker d^i/\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$.  A functor is left exact if it preserves
the left three terms of every short exact sequence.  An object is injective if
$\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$ is exact, and an injective resolution is an exact
embedding into a complex of injectives.  An object is $F$-acyclic if
$R^iF(A)=0$ for $i>0$; a category has enough injectives if every object embeds
in an injective object.  For a left exact functor $F$, the derived functors are
$R^iF(A)=H^i(F(I^\bullet))$ for an injective resolution $I^\bullet$.
nodes.title: Abelian category, complexes, and exact functors

nodes.statement:
If $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives and $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ is
additive left exact, then $R^iF(A)=H^i(F(I^\bullet))$ is independent of the
injective resolution and is functorial and additive.  There is a natural
isomorphism $R^0F\cong F$, and each short exact sequence
$0\to A'\to A\to A''\to0$ gives a functorial long exact sequence with
connecting maps $\delta^i:R^iF(A'')\to R^{i+1}F(A')$.  Morphisms of short
exact sequences commute with the connecting maps, and $R^iF(I)=0$ for
$i>0$ and $I$ injective.
nodes.title: Derived functors

nodes.statement:
If $0\to A\to J^0\to J^1\to\cdots$ is exact and every $J^i$ is
$F$-acyclic, then $R^iF(A)\cong H^i(F(J^\bullet))$ naturally.
nodes.title: Acyclic resolutions

nodes.statement:
A covariant $\delta$-functor is functors $T^i$ with connecting maps giving
long exact sequences and commuting with morphisms of short exact sequences.
It is universal if a map in degree zero to another $\delta$-functor extends
uniquely in every degree.  A functor is effaceable if every object embeds into
an object on which it vanishes.
nodes.title: Cohomological $\delta$-functor and universality

nodes.statement: An effaceable positive-degree $\delta$-functor is universal.
nodes.title: Effaceability criterion

nodes.statement:
For a left exact $F$ on a category with enough injectives, $(R^iF)$ is a
universal $\delta$-functor with degree zero $F$.  Conversely, every universal
$\delta$-functor has left exact degree zero and is naturally isomorphic to the
derived functors of that degree-zero functor.
nodes.title: Universal property of derived functors

nodes.statement: Every module over a ring embeds in an injective module.
nodes.title: Enough injectives for modules

nodes.statement:
For every ringed space $(X,\mathcal O_X)$, the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules
has enough injectives.
nodes.title: Enough injective sheaves

nodes.statement:
The category of sheaves of abelian groups on any topological space has enough
injectives.
nodes.title: Enough injective abelian sheaves

nodes.statement:
For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$, $H^i(X,\mathcal F)$ is the $i$th right
derived functor of $\Gamma(X,-)$.  A sheaf is flasque when all restriction
maps are surjective.
nodes.title: Sheaf cohomology and flasque sheaves

nodes.statement: Every injective $\mathcal O_X$-module is flasque.
nodes.title: Injectives are flasque

nodes.statement: If $\mathcal F$ is flasque, then $H^i(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for $i>0$.
nodes.title: Flasque acyclicity

nodes.statement:
The derived functors of $\Gamma(X,-)$ on $\mathcal O_X$-modules are the
groups $H^i(X,-)$ defined on abelian sheaves.
nodes.title: Global sections as derived functors

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is noetherian of dimension $n$, then $H^i(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for every
abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ and $i>n$.
nodes.title: Grothendieck vanishing

nodes.statement: On a noetherian space, a filtered direct limit of flasque sheaves is flasque.
nodes.title: Limits of flasque sheaves
Cohomology and direct limits

nodes.statement:
For a closed inclusion $j:Y\hookrightarrow X$,
$H^i(Y,\mathcal F)\cong H^i(X,j_*\mathcal F)$.
nodes.title: Closed-subset extension

nodes.statement:
If $A$ is noetherian, $M\subset N$ are finite $A$-modules and $\mathfrak a$
is an ideal, the $\mathfrak a$-adic topology on $M$ is induced from $N$.
nodes.title: Krull's theorem

nodes.statement:
For an injective $A$-module $I$, the submodule $\Gamma_{\mathfrak a}(I)$ of
$\mathfrak a$-power torsion is injective.
nodes.title: Torsion in an injective module

nodes.statement:
For injective $I$ over a noetherian ring, $I\to I_f$ is surjective for every
$f\in A$.
nodes.title: Localization of injectives

nodes.statement:
If $I$ is injective over noetherian $A$, then $\widetilde I$ on
$\operatorname{Spec}A$ is flasque.
nodes.title: Injective quasi-coherent sheaves are flasque

nodes.statement:
For $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ noetherian and $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent,
$H^i(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for $i>0$ and $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ recovers its
module.
nodes.title: Affine vanishing

nodes.statement:
Every quasi-coherent sheaf on a noetherian scheme embeds in a flasque
quasi-coherent sheaf.
nodes.title: Flasque quasi-coherent embedding
Serre's affineness criterion

nodes.statement:
For an ordered open cover $\mathfrak U=(U_i)$, set
$C^p(\mathfrak U,\mathcal F)=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_p}\mathcal F(U_{i_0\cdots i_p})$
with the alternating restriction differential, and define
$\check H^p(\mathfrak U,\mathcal F)=H^p(C^\bullet)$.
nodes.title: Cech complex

nodes.statement:
The canonical map $H^0(\mathfrak U,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ is an
isomorphism.
nodes.title: Cech degree zero

nodes.statement: The sheafified Cech complex is a resolution of $\mathcal F$.
nodes.title: Sheafified Cech resolution

nodes.statement:
If $\mathcal F$ is flasque, then $\check H^p(\mathfrak U,\mathcal F)=0$ for
$p>0$.
nodes.title: Flasque Cech acyclicity

nodes.statement:
There is a natural map $\check H^p(\mathfrak U,\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$,
functorial in $\mathcal F$.
nodes.title: Cech comparison map

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is noetherian separated, $\mathfrak U$ is an affine open cover, and
$\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, then the comparison map is an isomorphism in
every degree.
nodes.title: Cech comparison for affine covers
Cohomology of projective space

nodes.statement:
For $X$ projective over noetherian $A$ with a very ample $\mathcal O_X(1)$ and
$\mathcal F$ coherent, $H^i(X,\mathcal F)$ is finite over $A$, and
$H^i(X,\mathcal F(n))=0$ for $i>0$ and all $n\gg0$.
nodes.title: Serre finiteness and eventual vanishing

nodes.statement:
For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on a proper noetherian $A$-scheme,
$\mathcal L$ is ample iff for every coherent $\mathcal F$,
$H^i(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^n)=0$ for $i>0$ and $n\gg0$.
nodes.title: Cohomological criterion for ampleness

nodes.statement:
$\mathcal H om(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ is the sheaf of local homomorphisms,
and $\mathcal E xt^i(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ is the $i$th right derived
functor of $\mathcal H om(\mathcal F,-)$.  The groups
$\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ are the right derived
functors of $\operatorname{Hom}_X(\mathcal F,-)$.
nodes.title: Ext

nodes.statement: Injective sheaves remain injective after restriction to an open subset.
nodes.title: Restriction of injectives

nodes.statement:
For $U\subset X$, $\mathcal E xt_X^i(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)|_U\cong
\mathcal E xt_U^i(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal G|_U)$.
nodes.title: Restriction of sheaf Ext

nodes.statement:
$\mathcal E xt^0(\mathcal O_X,\mathcal G)=\mathcal G$, higher sheaf Ext from
$\mathcal O_X$ vanishes, and $\operatorname{Ext}^i(\mathcal O_X,\mathcal G)=H^i(X,\mathcal G)$.
nodes.title: Ext from the structure sheaf

nodes.statement:
A short exact sequence in the first variable gives the usual long exact
sequences for both global Ext and sheaf Ext.
nodes.title: Long exact Ext sequences

nodes.statement:
If $\mathcal F$ has a locally free finite-rank resolution $\mathcal L_\bullet$,
then $\mathcal E xt^i(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)=H^i(\mathcal H om(\mathcal L_\bullet,\mathcal G))$.
nodes.title: Locally free resolutions

nodes.statement:
If $\mathcal L$ is locally free of finite rank and $I$ injective, then
$\mathcal L\otimes I$ is injective.
nodes.title: Tensoring injectives

nodes.statement:
$\operatorname{Ext}^i(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L,\mathcal G)\cong
\operatorname{Ext}^i(\mathcal F,\mathcal L^\vee\otimes\mathcal G)$, and likewise for sheaf Ext.
nodes.title: Ext and locally free tensor factors

nodes.statement:
For coherent $\mathcal F$ on a noetherian scheme,
$(\mathcal E xt^i(\mathcal F,\mathcal G))_x\cong
\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal F_x,\mathcal G_x)$.
nodes.title: Stalks of sheaf Ext

nodes.statement:
For coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ on projective $X$, and fixed $i$, for
$n\gg0$ the natural maps from global sections of $\mathcal E xt^i(\mathcal F,\mathcal G(n))$
to $\operatorname{Ext}^i(\mathcal F,\mathcal G(n))$ are isomorphisms.
nodes.title: Ext twisting comparison

nodes.statement:
For a module, projective dimension is the length of its shortest projective
resolution.
nodes.title: Projective dimension

nodes.statement:
Over a regular local ring, finite projective dimension equals dimension minus
depth.
nodes.title: Regular local rings

nodes.statement: The Ext groups against the residue field detect the depth of a finite module.
nodes.title: Ext detects depth

nodes.statement:
For $X=\mathbf P_k^n$ and $\omega_X=\mathcal O_X(-n-1)$,
$H^n(X,\omega_X)\cong k$, the pairing
$\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\omega_X)\times H^n(X,\mathcal F)\to k$
is perfect, and $\operatorname{Ext}^i(\mathcal F,\omega_X)\cong
H^{n-i}(X,\mathcal F)^\vee$ for coherent $\mathcal F$.
nodes.title: Duality for projective space

nodes.statement:
For proper $n$-dimensional $X/k$, a dualizing sheaf is coherent $\omega_X$ with
a trace $H^n(X,\omega_X)\to k$ inducing perfect Hom--top-cohomology pairings.
nodes.title: Dualizing sheaf

nodes.statement:
A dualizing sheaf with trace is unique up to a unique trace-preserving
isomorphism.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of dualizing sheaves

nodes.statement:
If $X\subset\mathbf P^N$ has codimension $r$, then
$\mathcal E xt^i(\mathcal O_X,\omega_{\mathbf P^N})=0$ for $i<r$.
nodes.title: Ext vanishing by codimension

nodes.statement:
With $\omega_X=\mathcal E xt^r(\mathcal O_X,\omega_{\mathbf P^N})$,
$\operatorname{Hom}_X(\mathcal F,\omega_X)\cong
\operatorname{Ext}_{\mathbf P^N}^r(\mathcal F,\omega_{\mathbf P^N})$.
nodes.title: The dualizing Ext sheaf

nodes.statement: Every projective scheme over a field has a dualizing sheaf.
nodes.title: Existence of dualizing sheaves

nodes.statement:
For projective equidimensional $n$-fold $X/k$ with dualizing sheaf $\omega_X$,
there are natural maps $\operatorname{Ext}^i(\mathcal F,\omega_X)\to
H^{n-i}(X,\mathcal F)^\vee$.  They are all isomorphisms iff $X$ is
Cohen--Macaulay and equidimensional, equivalently iff every locally free
$\mathcal F$ has $H^i(X,\mathcal F(-q))=0$ for $i<n$ and $q\gg0$.
nodes.title: Duality for a projective scheme

nodes.statement:
For Cohen--Macaulay equidimensional projective $X$, duality holds for locally
free sheaves.
nodes.title: Cohen--Macaulay duality

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is normal of dimension at least two, then
$H^i(X,\mathcal F(-q))=0$ for $i<2$ and $q\gg0$.
nodes.title: Normal vanishing

nodes.statement:
An ample effective divisor on a normal projective variety of dimension at least
two is connected.
nodes.title: Connected ample divisors

nodes.statement:
If $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ is an $M$-regular sequence, the positive homology of its
Koszul complex with coefficients in $M$ vanishes and degree zero is
$M/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)M$.
nodes.title: Koszul regular sequence

nodes.statement:
If $X\subset\mathbf P^N$ is a codimension-$r$ local complete intersection with
ideal $\mathcal I$, then
$\omega_X\cong\omega_{\mathbf P^N}\otimes\bigwedge^r(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2)^\vee$;
it is invertible.
nodes.title: Dualizing sheaf of a local complete intersection

nodes.statement: For a nonsingular projective variety, $\omega_X$ is the canonical sheaf.
nodes.title: Canonical sheaf on a nonsingular variety

nodes.statement:
Serre duality holds with the canonical sheaf; in particular
$H^n(X,\omega_X)\cong k$ and for curves $p_a=p_g$.
nodes.title: Serre duality for nonsingular varieties

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be a complete nonsingular curve over an algebraically closed field
$k$, let $K$ be its function field, and let $\Omega_K$ be the space of
meromorphic differentials.  For each closed point $P$ there is a unique
$k$-linear map $\operatorname{res}_P:\Omega_K\to k$ such that, for a local
parameter $t$, $\operatorname{res}_P(t^n\,dt)=0$ for $n\ne-1$ and
$\operatorname{res}_P(t^{-1}dt)=1$.
nodes.title: Existence of residues

nodes.statement: For every $\omega\in\Omega_K$, $\sum_{P\in X}\operatorname{res}_P(\omega)=0$.
nodes.title: Residue theorem

nodes.statement: $R^if_*\mathcal F$ is the $i$th derived functor of direct image.
nodes.title: Higher direct image

nodes.statement:
The sheaf $R^if_*\mathcal F$ is the sheaf associated to
$U\mapsto H^i(f^{-1}U,\mathcal F)$.
nodes.title: Stalk description

nodes.statement:
Restriction to an open $V\subset Y$ identifies $(R^if_*\mathcal F)|_V$ with
$R^i(f|_{f^{-1}V})_*\mathcal F$.
nodes.title: Restriction of direct images

nodes.statement: $R^if_*$ vanishes on flasque sheaves.
nodes.title: Flasque vanishing

nodes.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of ringed spaces.  The functors $R^if_*$ on
sheaves of modules are the derived functors of
$f_*:\operatorname{Mod}(X)\to\operatorname{Mod}(Y)$.
nodes.title: Direct image on module categories

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be noetherian, let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, and let
$Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be affine.  For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ on
$X$ there is a natural isomorphism
\[
R^if_*\mathcal F\cong\widetilde{H^i(X,\mathcal F)}.
\]
nodes.title: Affine direct images

nodes.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes with $X$ noetherian.  If
$\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, then each $R^if_*\mathcal F$ is
quasi-coherent.
nodes.title: Quasi-coherence of direct images

nodes.statement:
In the separated noetherian case, higher direct images are computed on affine
covers by Cech complexes.
nodes.title: Separated affine computation

nodes.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be projective between noetherian schemes, let $\mathcal F$ be
coherent, and let $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_X(1)$ be very ample over $Y$.  Then
(a) for every $n>0$, the natural map
$f^*f_*\mathcal F(n)\to\mathcal F(n)$ is surjective; (b) each
$R^if_*\mathcal F$ is coherent; and (c) $R^if_*\mathcal F(n)=0$ for
$i>0$ and $n\gg0$.
nodes.title: Coherence of proper direct images

nodes.statement:
For an $A$-module $M$ the following hold: (a) $M$ is flat iff
$-\otimes_A M$ is exact; (b) base extension preserves flatness; (c) flatness
is transitive; (d) flatness is local under localization; (e) in a short exact
sequence, if two terms are flat then so is the third; and (f) a finite module
over a local noetherian ring is flat iff it is free.
nodes.title: Flatness criteria

nodes.statement: A morphism is flat when the induced local ring maps are flat.
nodes.title: Flat morphism

nodes.statement:
The properties of flat modules in Proposition~III.9.1A globalize: localization,
base change, and composition preserve flatness.
nodes.title: Localization and base change of flatness

nodes.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated morphism of finite type between noetherian
schemes, let $g:Y'\to Y$ be flat, and let $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projection
$g':X'\to X$.  Then, for quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$,
\[
g^*R^if_*\mathcal F\simeq R^ig'_*g'^*\mathcal F.
\]
nodes.title: Base change for quasi-coherent sheaves

nodes.statement:
If $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $y\in Y$ has residue field $k(y)$, then
\[
H^i(X,\mathcal F)\otimes_A k(y)\simeq H^i(X_y,\mathcal F_y)
\]
under the hypotheses of Proposition~III.9.3.
nodes.title: Affine flat base change

nodes.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of finite type over a field $k$, and assume
$f$ is flat.  Then for every $x\in X$, with $y=f(x)$,
\[
\dim_x(X_y)=\dim_xX-\dim_yY.
\]
nodes.title: Flatness and fiber dimensions

nodes.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat, of finite type over a field, with $Y$ irreducible.
If $Y$ is regular of dimension one, then the following are equivalent: every
associated point of $X$ maps to the generic point of $Y$, and every
irreducible component of every fiber has the expected dimension.
nodes.title: Flat families over regular curves

nodes.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism with $Y$ integral and regular of dimension one.
Then $f$ is flat iff every associated point of $X$ maps to the generic point
of $Y$; if $X$ is reduced, this is equivalent to every irreducible component
of $X$ dominating $Y$.
nodes.title: Flatness and associated points

nodes.statement:
Let $Y$ be a regular integral curve, let $P\in Y$ be closed, and let
$X\subset\mathbf P^n_{Y-P}$ be flat over $Y-P$.  The scheme-theoretic closure
$\overline X\subset\mathbf P^n_Y$ is flat over $Y$.
nodes.title: Flat closure over a curve

nodes.statement:
For an integral noetherian base $T$ and a flat projective family
$X\subset\mathbf P_T^n$, the Hilbert polynomial of the fibers is constant.
nodes.title: Flat families of projective schemes

nodes.statement: For connected bases the Hilbert polynomial is constant.
nodes.title: Constancy on connected bases

nodes.statement:
An algebraic family of normal varieties parametrized by a nonsingular curve is
a flat family of schemes.
nodes.title: Normal families over a nonsingular curve

nodes.statement:
For a local noetherian domain, the relevant intersection of principal ideals
in a flat finite-type algebra is controlled by the generic fiber; this gives
the specialization lemma used in the normal-family result.
nodes.title: Hironaka

nodes.statement:
In a flat family of normal projective varieties the arithmetic genus is
constant.
nodes.title: Normal-family genus

nodes.statement:
A finite-type morphism is smooth of relative dimension $n$ when it is flat and
its geometric fibers are nonsingular $n$-folds; equivalently it has the formal
lifting property and locally free relative differentials of rank $n$.
nodes.title: Smooth morphism

nodes.statement:
For $X\to Y\to Z$ there is a right-exact sequence
$f^*\Omega_{Y/Z}\to\Omega_{X/Z}\to\Omega_{X/Y}\to0$; smoothness is
characterized by local freeness of the last term together with flatness.
nodes.title: Differentials

nodes.statement:
For finite-type schemes over a field, smoothness is equivalent to the expected
rank condition on differentials/Jacobian at every point.
nodes.title: Jacobian criterion

nodes.statement:
The dimension, embedding dimension, and projective dimension relations for a
local homomorphism give the regularity criterion used in the smoothness proof.
nodes.title: Regular local algebra

nodes.statement: Composites and base changes of smooth morphisms are smooth.
nodes.title: Composition and base change for smooth maps

nodes.statement:
A dominant finite-type morphism of integral schemes is generically smooth
after removing the inseparable locus; in characteristic zero this holds
without a separability qualification.
nodes.title: Generic separability

nodes.statement: A dominant morphism of nonsingular varieties is smooth on a dense open set.
nodes.title: Generic smoothness

nodes.statement:
Over a perfect field, a finite-type morphism is smooth on a dense open when its
generic extension is separable.
nodes.title: Generic smoothness over a perfect field

nodes.statement:
A homogeneous space under an algebraic group is nonsingular, and its general
hyperplane sections satisfy the Bertini conclusion.
nodes.title: Homogeneous-space smoothness

nodes.statement:
A general hyperplane section of a nonsingular projective variety is
nonsingular under the stated characteristic hypotheses.
nodes.title: Bertini theorem

nodes.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be projective noetherian, $y\in Y$, and $\mathcal F$ coherent.
Writing $X_n=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^{n+1})$,
there is a natural isomorphism
\[\widehat{(R^if_*\mathcal F)}_y\cong\varprojlim_nH^i(X_n,\mathcal F|_{X_n}).\]
nodes.title: Theorem on formal functions

nodes.statement: The completed direct image is compatible with completion and base change.
nodes.title: Completion and base change

nodes.statement: In the affine case, the completed direct-image modules are finite.
nodes.title: Affine formal functions

nodes.statement:
A proper birational morphism to a normal scheme has
$f_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$.
nodes.title: Zariski main theorem

nodes.statement:
A proper morphism factors through a finite morphism after taking the relative
Spec of its direct-image algebra.
nodes.title: Stein factorization

nodes.statement:
For a bounded complex of finite free modules over a noetherian ring, its
cohomology after tensoring with a residue field is represented by a bounded
complex of finite free modules with differentials in the maximal ideal.
nodes.title: Universal complexes

nodes.statement:
The resulting fiber dimensions are controlled by the ranks of the
differentials.
nodes.title: Fiber dimensions of complexes

nodes.statement:
Over a local ring, a complex with differentials in the maximal ideal has fiber
cohomology whose dimension is the rank of the corresponding free term minus
the ranks of adjacent differentials.
nodes.title: Minimal complexes

nodes.statement:
For a complex of finite free modules, the following are equivalent: a fiber
cohomology dimension is locally constant; the relevant cohomology module is
free and commutes with residue-field base change; and the neighboring
differential has the required constant rank.
nodes.title: Equivalent complex conditions

nodes.statement:
There is a natural map from the cohomology of a finite complex tensored with
$k(y)$ to the cohomology of the tensor complex, and its kernel/cokernel are
controlled by the neighboring cohomology module.
nodes.title: Natural fiber map

nodes.statement:
Constancy of the relevant fiber dimension makes the cohomology module locally
free and makes the fiber map an isomorphism.
nodes.title: Local freeness criterion

nodes.statement:
A function is upper semicontinuous when each locus where its value is at most a
fixed integer is open.
nodes.title: Upper semicontinuity

nodes.statement:
For projective $f:X\to Y$ with $Y$ noetherian and coherent $\mathcal F$ flat
over $Y$, $y\mapsto\dim_{k(y)}H^i(X_y,\mathcal F_y)$ is upper semicontinuous.
nodes.title: Semicontinuity

nodes.statement:
If a fiber cohomology dimension is constant near $y$, $R^if_*\mathcal F$ is
locally free there and commutes with arbitrary residue-field base change.
nodes.title: Grauert and base change

nodes.statement:
The base-change map $(R^if_*\mathcal F)\otimes k(y)\to H^i(X_y,\mathcal F_y)$
is surjective precisely under the neighboring-map condition; if it is
surjective, it is an isomorphism near $y$ and $R^{i-1}f_*\mathcal F$ is locally
free there.
nodes.title: Cohomology and base change criterion

nodes.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be projective, $Y$ noetherian, and $\mathcal F$ coherent and
flat over $Y$.  The natural map
$(R^if_*\mathcal F)\otimes k(y)\to H^i(X_y,\mathcal F_y)$ is an isomorphism
near $y$ whenever the degree-$i$ map is surjective at $y$; in that case the
preceding direct image is locally free near $y$.
nodes.title: Cohomology and base change

nodes.statement:
A curve is a complete nonsingular integral curve over an algebraically closed
field \(k\).  For \(D=\sum n_PP\), put
\(\deg D=\sum n_P\), \(\mathcal L(D)=\{f:(f)+D\ge0\}\cup\{0\}\), and
\(l(D)=h^0(X,\mathcal L(D))\).  The complete system \(|D|\) is
\(\mathbf P(H^0(X,\mathcal L(D)))\), of dimension \(l(D)-1\).
nodes.title: Curves and divisors

nodes.statement: \(p_a(X)=p_g(X)=h^1(X,\mathcal O_X)=:g\).
nodes.title: Genus

nodes.statement: If \(l(D)\ne0\), then \(\deg D\ge0\); if also \(\deg D=0\), then \(D\sim0\).
nodes.title: Degree zero

nodes.statement:
For finite \(f:X\to Y\), \(e_P=v_P(t)\) for a parameter \(t\) at \(f(P)\).
Ramification means \(e_P>1\), and it is tame if characteristic zero or
\(p\nmid e_P\).  Separability means \(K(X)/K(Y)\) is separable.
nodes.title: Ramification

nodes.statement:
For a divisor $D$ on a complete nonsingular curve, write
$\mathcal L(D)=\{f\in K(X):(f)+D\ge0\}\cup\{0\}$ and
$l(D)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal L(D))$.  The complete linear system is
$|D|=\mathbf P H^0(X,\mathcal L(D))$; a linear system is base-point-free if
no point belongs to every member, and very ample if it separates points and
tangent vectors.  A divisor is ample precisely when it has positive degree.
nodes.title: Divisors and linear systems

nodes.statement:
\[
0\to f^*\Omega_Y\to\Omega_X\to\Omega_{X/Y}\to0.
\]
nodes.title: Differential sequence

nodes.statement:
\(\Omega_{X/Y}\) is torsion supported exactly at ramification points, and
\(\length(\Omega_{X/Y})_P=v_P(dt/du)\).  This equals \(e_P-1\) tamely and is
larger than \(e_P-1\) wildly.
nodes.title: Different

nodes.statement:
\[
K_X\sim f^*K_Y+R,\qquad
R=\sum_P\length(\Omega_{X/Y})_P\,P.
\]
nodes.title: Canonical divisors

nodes.statement:
\[
2g(X)-2=(\deg f)(2g(Y)-2)+\deg R,
\]
and tamely \(\deg R=\sum(e_P-1)\).
nodes.title: Hurwitz

nodes.statement:
If \(K(X)/K(Y)\) is purely inseparable, \(X,Y\) are abstractly isomorphic,
\(f\) is a composite of relative Frobenius maps, and \(g(X)=g(Y)\).
nodes.title: Purely inseparable maps

nodes.statement:
\(|D|\) is base-point-free iff \(\dim|D-P|=\dim|D|-1\) for all \(P\); \(D\)
is very ample iff \(\dim|D-P-Q|=\dim|D|-2\) for all \(P,Q\), including
\(P=Q\).
nodes.title: Linear systems

nodes.statement:
\(\deg D\ge2g\) implies no base points, and \(\deg D\ge2g+1\) implies very
ample.
nodes.title: Numerical bounds

nodes.statement: \(D\) is ample iff \(\deg D>0\).
nodes.title: Ample divisors

nodes.statement:
Projection from \(O\notin X\subset\mathbf P^n\) is a closed immersion iff
\(O\) lies on no secant and no tangent line of \(X\).
nodes.title: Projection criterion

nodes.statement:
If \(X\subset\mathbf P^n\) is a curve and \(n\ge4\), some projection embeds it
in \(\mathbf P^{n-1}\).
nodes.title: Projection dimension

nodes.statement: Every curve embeds in \(\mathbf P^3\).
nodes.title: Embedding in \(\mathbf P^3\)

nodes.statement:
Projection from \(O\in\mathbf P^3\) is birational with at most nodes iff \(O\)
lies on finitely many secants, no tangent or multisecant, and no secant with
coplanar tangent lines.
nodes.title: Nodal projection

nodes.statement:
If every secant of a nonplanar curve is a multisecant, or every pair of
tangents is coplanar, then one point lies on every tangent.
nodes.title: Tangent degeneracy

nodes.statement:
The only strange curves in projective space are a line and a characteristic-two
conic.
nodes.title: Samuel

nodes.statement:
Every curve in \(\mathbf P^3\) projects birationally to a plane curve with at
most nodes.
nodes.title: Plane nodal model

nodes.statement: Every curve is birationally equivalent to a plane curve with at most nodes.
nodes.title: Birational nodal model

nodes.statement:
An elliptic curve is a genus-one curve with chosen \(P_0\).  In characteristic
\(\ne2\), normalize the four branch points to \(0,1,\lambda,\infty\), and set
\(j=2^8(\lambda^2-\lambda+1)^3/(\lambda^2(\lambda-1)^2)\).
nodes.title: Elliptic curve

nodes.statement:
An elliptic curve is a genus-one curve with a chosen origin $P_0$.  Its
degree-zero Picard functor is represented by the Jacobian.  For a nonsingular
curve of genus $g\ge2$, the canonical divisor is represented by
$\Omega_X$, and the canonical linear system is $|K|$.
nodes.title: Elliptic and canonical data

nodes.statement:
Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic \(\ne2\), \(j\) is
intrinsic, classifies elliptic curves up to isomorphism, and every element
occurs.
nodes.title: The \(j\)-invariant

nodes.statement:
For \(P,Q\in X\), an involution \(\sigma\) satisfies
\(\sigma(P)=Q\) and \(R+\sigma(R)\sim P+Q\).
nodes.title: Involution

nodes.statement: \(\operatorname{Aut}X\) acts transitively on \(X\).
nodes.title: Transitivity

nodes.statement:
Any two degree-two maps \(f_1,f_2:X\to\mathbf P^1\) satisfy
\(f_2\sigma=\tau f_1\) for source and target automorphisms \(\sigma,\tau\).
nodes.title: Degree-two maps

nodes.statement:
The orbit is \(\lambda,\lambda^{-1},1-\lambda,(1-\lambda)^{-1},
\lambda/(\lambda-1),(\lambda-1)/\lambda\).
nodes.title: Cross-ratio orbit

nodes.statement:
In characteristic \(\ne2\), \(X\) embeds as
\(y^2=x(x-1)(x-\lambda)\), with \(P_0=(0,1,0)\), and \(\lambda\) is defined
up to the preceding orbit.
nodes.title: Legendre equation

nodes.statement:
\(|\operatorname{Aut}(X,P_0)|\) is \(2,4,6,12\) in the four \(j\)/characteristic
cases displayed in the book.
nodes.title: Automorphism orders

nodes.statement: Negation and addition \(X\times X\to X\) are morphisms.
nodes.title: Group law morphisms

nodes.statement: Every morphism of elliptic curves preserving origins is a group homomorphism.
nodes.title: Homomorphism

nodes.statement:
For characteristic \(\ne2\), \(\mathbf Z\hookrightarrow\operatorname{End}(X,P_0)\),
and every nonzero integer endomorphism is finite.
nodes.title: Integer endomorphisms

nodes.statement:
The elliptic curve with
\(\mathcal L=\mathcal L(\Delta)\otimes p_1^*\mathcal L(-P_0)\) represents its
degree-zero Picard functor and has the divisor-law group structure.
nodes.title: Jacobian

nodes.statement:
The elliptic-function field is generated by \(\wp,\wp'\), satisfying
\((\wp')^2=4\wp^3-g_2\wp-g_3\).  Proof cited to Hurwitz--Courant.
nodes.title: Weierstrass functions

nodes.statement:
\(\sum n_i(a_i)\) is a principal divisor on \(\mathbf C/\Lambda\) iff
\(\sum n_i=0\) and \(\sum n_i a_i=0\). Proof cited.
nodes.title: Elliptic divisors

nodes.statement:
Every nonzero-discriminant pair \(c_2,c_3\) is realized by a lattice up to
scaling. Proof cited.
nodes.title: Lattice realization

nodes.statement:
\(J(\tau)=J(\tau')\) iff \(\tau'=(a\tau+b)/(c\tau+d)\) with
\(ad-bc=\pm1\), and each value has a unique representative in \(G\). Proof
cited.
nodes.title: Modular classification

nodes.statement:
\(X(\mathbf C)\cong\mathbf R/\mathbf Z\times\mathbf R/\mathbf Z\), with
\(n\)-torsion \((\mathbf Z/n)^2\).
nodes.title: Complex group

nodes.statement:
Multiplication by \(n\) is finite of degree \(n^2\), since its kernel has that
order and it is separable.
nodes.title: Multiplication

nodes.statement:
Endomorphisms correspond injectively as a ring to \(\alpha\) with
\(\alpha\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda\).
nodes.title: Analytic endomorphisms

nodes.statement:
Complex multiplication occurs iff \(\tau\in\mathbf Q(\sqrt{-d})\), and the
endomorphism ring is the order specified by the integral conditions
\(2br,b(r^2+ds^2)\in\mathbf Z\) for \(\tau=r+s\sqrt{-d}\).
nodes.title: Complex multiplication

nodes.statement:
Only countably many complex \(j\)-values have complex multiplication, since
there are countably many imaginary quadratic orders.
nodes.title: CM count

nodes.statement:
For a cubic \(f=0\), Hasse invariant zero iff the coefficient of
\((xyz)^{p-1}\) in \(f^{p-1}\) is zero.
nodes.title: Hasse coefficient

nodes.statement:
For \(y^2=x(x-1)(x-\lambda)\), Hasse zero iff
\(\sum_{i=0}^{(p-1)/2}{(p-1)/2\choose i}^2\lambda^i=0\).
nodes.title: Hasse polynomial

nodes.statement: There are at most \(\lfloor p/12\rfloor+2\) supersingular \(j\)'s.
nodes.title: Supersingular count

nodes.statement: If \(g\ge2\), \(|K|\) has no base points.
nodes.title: Canonical base points

nodes.statement: \(|K|\) is very ample iff \(X\) is nonhyperelliptic.
nodes.title: Canonical very ampleness

nodes.statement:
For a hyperelliptic genus-\(g\) curve, the \(g^1_2\) is unique, the canonical
map has degree two onto a rational normal curve of degree \(g-1\), and
\(|K|\) is the sum of \(g-1\) fibres.
nodes.title: Hyperelliptic canonical map

nodes.statement:
For effective special \(D\), \(\dim|D|\le\frac12\deg D\), with equality only
for \(0,K\), or hyperelliptic multiples of the unique \(g^1_2\).
nodes.title: Clifford

nodes.statement: \(\dim|D|+\dim|E|\le\dim|D+E|\) for effective \(D,E\).
nodes.title: Addition of systems

nodes.statement:
For \(g\ge2\), a nonspecial very ample divisor of degree \(d\) exists iff
\(d\ge g+3\).
nodes.title: Halphen

nodes.statement:
Such a curve in \(\mathbf P^3\) exists iff \(g=0,d\ge1\), \(g=1,d\ge3\), or
\(g\ge2,d\ge g+3\).
nodes.title: Space-curve existence

nodes.statement:
For a nonplanar curve with special hyperplane section, \(d\ge6\) and
\(g\ge d/2+1\); for \(d=6\) it is the canonical genus-four curve.
nodes.title: Special hyperplane section

nodes.statement:
\[
g\le\begin{cases}\frac14d^2-d+1&d\text{ even},\\
\frac14(d^2-1)-d+1&d\text{ odd}.\end{cases}
\]
Equality is attained for every \(d\ge3\), and equality curves lie on quadrics.
nodes.title: Castelnuovo

nodes.statement: $A(X)$ is a commutative associative graded ring with identity.
nodes.title: Chow-ring structure

nodes.statement: Pullback is a ring map and $(gf)^*=f^*g^*$.
nodes.title: Functorial pullback

nodes.statement: Proper pushforward is graded and $(gf)_*=g_*f_*$.
nodes.title: Functorial proper pushforward

nodes.statement: For the diagonal $\Delta:X\to X\times X$, $YZ=\Delta^*(Y\times Z)$.
nodes.title: Diagonal formula

nodes.statement:
If $Y,Z$ meet properly, $YZ=\sum_W i(Y,Z;W)W$, with $i(Y,Z;W)$ local at the
generic point of $W$.
nodes.title: Proper-intersection multiplicities

nodes.statement:
If $Z$ is an effective Cartier divisor meeting $Y$ properly, $YZ$ is the cycle
of the Cartier divisor cut on $Y$.
nodes.title: Cartier-divisor normalization

nodes.statement:
On nonsingular quasi-projective varieties there is a unique intersection
theory satisfying A1--A7.  For proper intersection, the local multiplicity is
\[
i(Y,Z;W)=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j\length_A\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(A/\mathfrak a,A/\mathfrak b),
\]
where $A=\mathcal O_{X,\eta_W}$ and $\mathfrak a,\mathfrak b$ are the ideals
of $Y,Z$.  Chow's moving lemma says that $Z$ is rationally equivalent to a
cycle meeting $Y$ properly, and two such choices give the same product.
nodes.title: Intersection theory

nodes.statement: $A^1(X)\simeq\operatorname{Pic}X$.
nodes.title: Divisors and the Picard group

nodes.statement:
Projection $X\times\mathbb A^n\to X$ induces
$A(X)\simeq A(X\times\mathbb A^n)$.
nodes.title: Affine-space invariance

nodes.statement:
For a nonsingular closed $Y\subset X$, with $U=X-Y$, the sequence
$A(Y)\to A(X)\to A(U)\to0$ is exact.
nodes.title: Localization

nodes.statement:
If $\mathcal E$ has rank $r$, then $A(\mathbb P(\mathcal E))$ is a free
$A(X)$-module on $1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^{r-1}$, where $\xi$ is the tautological
divisor class.
nodes.title: Projective-bundle formula

nodes.statement: $c(\mathcal O_X(D))=1+D$.
nodes.title: First Chern class of a line bundle

nodes.statement: $c_i(f^*\mathcal E)=f^*c_i(\mathcal E)$.
nodes.title: Pullback of Chern classes

nodes.statement:
For $0\to\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E''\to0$,
$c(\mathcal E)=c(\mathcal E')c(\mathcal E'')$.
nodes.title: Whitney sum formula

nodes.statement:
If $\mathcal E$ has a filtration with invertible quotients $\mathcal L_i$,
then $c(\mathcal E)=\prod_i(1+c_1(\mathcal L_i))$.
nodes.title: Splitting principle

nodes.statement:
Under formal Chern roots $a_i,b_j$,
$c(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F)=\prod_{i,j}(1+(a_i+b_j)t)$,
$c(\bigwedge^p\mathcal E)=\prod_{|I|=p}(1+(\sum_{i\in I}a_i)t)$, and
$c(\mathcal E^\vee)=\prod_i(1-a_it)$.
nodes.title: Chern-root identities

nodes.statement:
If a section of $\mathcal E$ has zero scheme $Y$ of codimension $r$, then
$c_r(\mathcal E)=[Y]$.
nodes.title: Zero scheme of a section

nodes.statement:
If $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ is nonsingular of codimension $r$, then
$i_*c_r(N_{Y/X})=Y\cdot Y$.
nodes.title: Self-intersection formula

nodes.statement:
If $\mathcal E$ is locally free on a nonsingular projective $n$-fold $X$,
\[
\chi(\mathcal E)=\deg\bigl(\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)\operatorname{td}(T_X)\bigr)_n.
\]
nodes.title: Hirzebruch--Riemann--Roch

nodes.statement:
For a Cartier divisor $D$ on a scheme $X$ proper over an algebraically closed
field, $D$ is ample iff
$D^{\dim Y}\cdot Y>0$ for every positive-dimensional integral closed
subvariety $Y\subset X$.
nodes.title: Nakai--Moishezon criterion

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is a nonsingular projective surface, $H$ is ample, and $D$ is a
numerically nonzero divisor, then
\[
(D\cdot H)^2\geq (H^2)(D^2),
\]
with equality if and only if $D$ is numerically proportional to $H$.
nodes.title: Hodge index theorem

nodes.statement:
For a smooth projective morphism $f:X\to Y$ of nonsingular quasi-projective
varieties and $x\in K(X)$,
\[
\operatorname{ch}(f_!x)\operatorname{td}(T_Y)
=f_*\bigl(\operatorname{ch}(x)\operatorname{td}(T_X)\bigr).
\]
nodes.title: Grothendieck--Riemann--Roch

abbrev Sheaf (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] (X : TopCat.{w}) :=
  TopCat.Sheaf C X

abbrev IsSheaf {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {X : TopCat.{w}}

abbrev Presheaf (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] (X : TopCat.{w}) :=

nodes.statement:
A presheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ assigns an object $\mathcal F(U)$ to every open $U$ and restriction maps
$\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(V)$ for $V\subset U$, functorially, with $\mathcal F(\varnothing)=0$.
It is a sheaf when sections that agree locally glue uniquely. The definitions apply to sets,
abelian groups, rings, and modules.
More explicitly, if $\{U_i\}$ covers $U$, then restriction to the $U_i$ is injective, and every
family $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ satisfying
$s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}$ comes from a unique $s\in\mathcal F(U)$.
nodes.title: Presheaf and sheaf

def germ {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {X : TopCat.{v}} [HasColimits C]
    (F : Presheaf C X) (U : Opens X) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U) :
    F.obj (op U) ⟶ Stalk F x :=
  TopCat.Presheaf.germ F U x hx

def stalkMap {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {X : TopCat.{v}}
    {F G : Presheaf C X} [HasColimits C] (φ : F ⟶ G) (x : X) :
    Stalk F x ⟶ Stalk G x :=
  (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor C x).map φ

abbrev Stalk {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {X : TopCat.{v}}
    (F : Presheaf C X) [HasColimits C] (x : X) : C :=
  TopCat.Presheaf.stalk F x

@[reassoc] theorem germ_restrict {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {X : TopCat.{v}}
    [HasColimits C]
    (F : Presheaf C X) {U V : Opens X} (i : U ⟶ V) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U) :
    F.map i.op ≫ germ F U x hx = germ F V x (i.le hx) := by
  exact TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res F i x hx
nodes.statement:
The stalk is $\mathcal F_x=\varinjlim_{x\in U}\mathcal F(U)$. A morphism is a compatible family
of maps on opens and induces maps on stalks.  A germ is represented by a pair $(U,s)$ with $x\in U$;
$(U,s)$ and $(V,t)$ define the same germ exactly when $s$ and $t$ agree on some neighborhood of $x$
contained in $U\cap V$.
nodes.title: Stalks and morphisms

theorem sheaf_iso_iff_stalkMap_iso
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {X : TopCat.{v}}

For a continuous $f:X\to Y$, define $(f_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}V)$. The inverse image
$f^{-1}\mathcal G$ is the sheafification of $U\mapsto\varinjlim_{f(U)\subset V}\mathcal G(V)$.

nodes.statement:
A subsheaf $\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F$ is a sheaf whose sections are subgroups of the
sections of $\mathcal F$ and whose restrictions are induced.  The kernel of a sheaf morphism is its
sectionwise kernel, the image is the sheaf associated to its sectionwise image, and a morphism is
injective or surjective according as its kernel is zero or its image is the target.  A sequence is
exact when the image at every term equals the kernel at that term.  The quotient $\mathcal F/\mathcal F'$
is the sheaf associated to $U\mapsto\mathcal F(U)/\mathcal F'(U)$, with stalks
$(\mathcal F/\mathcal F')_x=\mathcal F_x/\mathcal F'_x$.
nodes.title: Subsheaves, exactness, and quotients
