@[simp]
nodes.statement:
$\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally ringed. A ring map $A\to B$ induces
$\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and every morphism
$\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ arises uniquely in this way.
nodes.title: Affine schemes and ring maps

nodes.statement:
An affine scheme is a locally ringed space isomorphic to an affine spectrum; a scheme is locally
affine. Open subschemes have restricted structure sheaves. A closed immersion is a homeomorphism
onto a closed subset with surjective structure-sheaf map.
nodes.title: Scheme and subschemes

nodes.statement:
Schemes and morphisms glue from affine open charts and compatible overlap isomorphisms satisfying
the cocycle condition.
nodes.title: Gluing schemes

nodes.statement:
For a graded ring $S$, $\operatorname{Proj}S$ is the homogeneous-prime space excluding the irrelevant
ideal, with basic opens $D_+(f)$, and structure sheaf given by degree-zero localizations.
nodes.title: Proj

nodes.statement:
The $D_+(f)$ form an affine open cover of $\operatorname{Proj}S$ and
$\Gamma(D_+(f),\mathcal O)=S_{(f)}$.
nodes.title: Proj charts

nodes.statement:
For a field $k$, a morphism $X\to\mathbb P^n_k$ is equivalent to an invertible sheaf $L$ on $X$ and
global sections $s_0,\ldots,s_n$ generating $L$, up to simultaneous multiplication by an isomorphism.
nodes.title: Projective space represents line bundles

nodes.statement:
A scheme is connected or irreducible according to its topological space, reduced when all affine
rings are reduced, integral when reduced and irreducible, and locally Noetherian when it has a cover
by spectra of Noetherian rings. An integral scheme is normal if its local rings are integrally closed.
nodes.title: Connected, reduced, integral, normal

nodes.statement: A scheme is integral iff it is reduced and irreducible.
nodes.title: Integral schemes

nodes.statement:
A scheme is locally Noetherian iff every affine open has Noetherian coordinate ring; an affine scheme
is Noetherian iff its coordinate ring is Noetherian.
nodes.title: Noetherian schemes

nodes.statement:
A morphism is locally of finite type when affine chart rings are finitely generated algebras, of
finite type when finitely many charts suffice over each affine target, and finite when inverse images
of affine opens are affine with finite module coordinate rings.
nodes.title: Morphisms of finite type and finite

nodes.statement:
Dimension is the supremum of chains of irreducible closed subsets; codimension is the supremum of
chains beginning at a given irreducible closed subset. For $\operatorname{Spec}A$ this is Krull dimension.
nodes.title: Dimension and codimension

nodes.statement:
For schemes $X,Y$ over $S$, $X\times_S Y$ exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism; for affine
schemes it is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RB)$.
nodes.title: Fibred products

nodes.statement:
For $f:X\to Y$ and $y\in Y$, $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$. Base extension is
$X_{S'}=X\times_SS'$. Fibres and base extensions are associative up to canonical isomorphism.
nodes.title: Fibres and base extension

nodes.statement: A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is separated when its diagonal $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_YX$ is a closed immersion.
nodes.title: Separated morphism

nodes.statement: Every morphism of affine schemes is separated.
nodes.title: Affine morphisms are separated

nodes.statement:
A morphism is separated iff its restriction over every member of an open affine cover of the target is
separated.
nodes.title: Separatedness is local on the target

nodes.statement:
For a finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f$ is separated iff for every valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $K$,
a diagram $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$ has at most one extension
$\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$.
nodes.title: Valuative criterion for separatedness

nodes.statement:
Let $R$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and
$U=\operatorname{Spec}K$. A map $U\to X$ is a point $x_\eta$ with $k(x_\eta)=K$; a map
$T\to X$ is points $x_\eta,x_0$ with $x_0$ a specialization of $x_\eta$ and an inclusion
$k(x_\eta)=K$ such that $R$ dominates the local ring of $x_0$ on its reduced irreducible closure.
nodes.title: Valuation-ring diagrams

nodes.statement:
For a quasi-compact morphism $f:X\to Y$, the image $f(X)$ is closed if and only if it is stable
under specialization.
nodes.title: Quasi-compact image criterion

nodes.statement:
For noetherian schemes: open and closed immersions are separated; compositions, products over a
base, and base changes of separated morphisms are separated; if $gf$ is separated then $f$ is
separated when $g$ is separated; and separatedness is local on the target.
nodes.title: Stability of separated morphisms

nodes.statement: A morphism is proper if it is separated, of finite type, and universally closed.
nodes.title: Proper morphism

nodes.statement:
For a finite-type morphism f, properness is equivalent to existence and uniqueness of a lift in every
valuation-ring diagram as above.
nodes.title: Valuative criterion for properness

nodes.statement: Proper morphisms are stable under composition and arbitrary base change; finite morphisms are proper.
nodes.title: Stability of properness

nodes.statement: A projective morphism of Noetherian schemes is proper.
nodes.title: Projective morphisms are proper

nodes.statement:
Over an algebraically closed field, the functor from varieties of Chapter I to schemes has image
the quasi-projective integral schemes of finite type; projective varieties correspond to projective
integral schemes. In particular the associated scheme of a variety is integral, separated, and of
finite type.
nodes.title: Varieties as schemes

nodes.statement:
An abstract variety is an integral separated scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed
field. A proper abstract variety is complete.
nodes.title: Abstract variety

nodes.statement:
If $A$ is a subring of a field $K$, the integral closure of $A$ in $K$ is the intersection of all
valuation rings of $K$ containing $A$.
nodes.title: Integral closure by valuation rings

nodes.statement:
For an $A$-module $M$, define $\widetilde M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by
$\widetilde M(D(f))=M_f$. An $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent if it is locally of this form, and
coherent on a Noetherian scheme if the modules are finitely generated.
nodes.title: Modules and associated sheaves

nodes.statement:
For $\operatorname{Spec}A$, $(\widetilde M)_\mathfrak p=M_\mathfrak p$ and
$\Gamma(D(f),\widetilde M)=M_f$. The map $M\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\widetilde M)$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.title: Basic affine module identities

nodes.statement:
If $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, then $M\mapsto\widetilde M$ is an equivalence between $A$-modules and
quasi-coherent sheaves, with quasi-inverse $\Gamma(X,-)$. For $A\to B$,
$f^*\widetilde M=\widetilde{M\otimes_AB}$.
nodes.title: Quasi-coherent sheaves on affines

nodes.statement:
If $f\in A$ and $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, then
$\Gamma(D(f),\mathcal F)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)_f$.
nodes.title: Localization criterion

nodes.statement:
An $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent iff it is locally the cokernel of a morphism between free
modules; on a Noetherian scheme it is coherent iff the free modules may be chosen finite rank.
nodes.title: Local characterization

nodes.statement: The functors $M\mapsto\widetilde M$ and $\Gamma$ are mutually inverse on quasi-coherent sheaves.
nodes.title: Affine equivalence

nodes.statement:
For an affine scheme, a sequence of quasi-coherent sheaves is exact iff the sequence of global-section
modules is exact.
nodes.title: Exactness on affines

nodes.statement:
Kernels, cokernels, images, and extensions of quasi-coherent sheaves are quasi-coherent; on a
Noetherian scheme the same holds for coherent sheaves.
nodes.title: Operations on quasi-coherent modules

nodes.statement:
For $f:X\to Y$, inverse images of quasi-coherent sheaves are quasi-coherent. Direct images are
quasi-coherent when X is Noetherian or f is quasi-compact and separated; in the Noetherian case
coherence is preserved by $f^*$.
nodes.title: Direct and inverse image of modules

nodes.statement:
The ideal sheaf of a closed subscheme is quasi-coherent, coherent when X is Noetherian, and every
quasi-coherent ideal sheaf is the ideal sheaf of a unique closed subscheme.
nodes.title: Ideal sheaves and closed subschemes

nodes.statement:
Ideals of $A$ are in bijection with closed subschemes of $\operatorname{Spec}A$; every such closed subscheme
is affine.
nodes.title: Affine closed subschemes

nodes.statement:
For graded $S$ and $M$, the associated sheaf on $\operatorname{Proj}S$ satisfies
$\Gamma(D_+(f),\widetilde M)=M_{(f)}$. It is quasi-coherent.
nodes.title: Proj modules

nodes.statement:
The sheaf $\mathcal O_X(n)=\widetilde{S(n)}$ on $X=\operatorname{Proj}S$ is invertible when $X$ is
covered by standard affine charts; $\mathcal O_X(m)\otimes\mathcal O_X(n)\simeq\mathcal O_X(m+n)$.
nodes.title: Twisting sheaves

nodes.statement:
For $S=A[x_0,\ldots,x_r]$ and $X=\operatorname{Proj}S=\mathbb P^r_A$, $\mathcal O_X(1)$ is invertible and
its coordinate sections generate it. A coherent sheaf on a projective scheme is generated after a
sufficiently positive twist.
nodes.title: Generation and projective embedding

nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal L$ be invertible on $X$, let $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$, and let $X_s$ be the
open set where $s$ is nonvanishing. If $X$ is quasi-compact and a section of a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal F$ vanishes on $X_s$, then some power of $s$ kills it. If $X$ has a finite affine cover
on which $\mathcal L$ is free and whose pairwise intersections are quasi-compact, every section
of $\mathcal F|_{X_s}$ becomes the restriction of a global section of $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^n$
after multiplying by a sufficiently high power of $s$.
nodes.title: Twisted localization

nodes.statement:
If $S$ is generated by $S_1$ over $S_0$, $X=\operatorname{Proj}S$, and $\mathcal F$ is
quasi-coherent, then the natural map $\widetilde{\Gamma_*(\mathcal F)}\to\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.title: Proj reconstruction

nodes.statement:
If $Y$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbb P^r_A$, it is $\operatorname{Proj}(S/I)$ for a homogeneous
ideal $I\subset S=A[x_0,\ldots,x_r]$. A scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is projective iff it is
isomorphic to $\operatorname{Proj}S$ for a graded $S$ with $S_0=A$ finitely generated by $S_1$.
nodes.title: Projective schemes as Proj

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is projective over a Noetherian ring $A$ and $\mathcal F$ is coherent, then
$\mathcal F(n)$ is generated by global sections for $n\gg0$ and $H^i(X,\mathcal F(n))=0$ for $i>0,n\gg0$.
nodes.title: Serre

nodes.statement:
On a projective scheme over a Noetherian ring, every coherent sheaf is a quotient of a finite direct
sum of twisted structure sheaves $\mathcal O_X(n)$.
nodes.title: Coherent sheaves are quotients of twists

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is projective over a field $k$ and $\mathcal F$ is coherent, then $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ is finite-dimensional
over k. If X is projective over a finitely generated k-algebra A, it is a finite A-module.
nodes.title: Finiteness of global sections

nodes.statement:
If $f:X\to Y$ is projective of finite type over a field and $\mathcal F$ is coherent, then
$f_*\mathcal F$ is coherent.
nodes.title: Coherent direct image

nodes.statement:
On a Noetherian integral scheme regular in codimension one, a prime divisor is an integral closed
subscheme of codimension one. A Weil divisor is a finite sum $D=\sum n_Y Y$. The local ring at the
generic point of $Y$ is a DVR, giving $v_Y:K(X)^*\to\mathbb Z$.
nodes.title: Weil divisors

nodes.statement:
For $f\in K(X)^*$, $(f)=\sum_Yv_Y(f)Y$ has finite support. Principal divisors form a subgroup of Weil
divisors.
nodes.title: Principal divisors

nodes.statement: $D\sim D'$ when $D-D'=(f)$. The class group is $\operatorname{Cl}X=\operatorname{Div}X/\operatorname{Prin}X$.
nodes.title: Linear equivalence and class group

nodes.statement:
Let $A$ be a noetherian domain and $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$.  Then $A$ is a
unique factorization domain if and only if $X$ is normal and $\operatorname{Cl}X=0$.
nodes.title: Factoriality and the divisor class group

nodes.statement:
If $A$ is an integrally closed noetherian domain, then
\[
A=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}A_{\mathfrak p}
\]
inside the fraction field of $A$, where the intersection runs over all height-one prime ideals.
nodes.title: Intersection of height-one localizations

nodes.statement:
A Cartier divisor is a compatible collection of rational functions modulo units. It determines an
invertible sheaf $\mathcal O_X(D)$; addition corresponds to tensor product and principal divisors give
$\mathcal O_X((f))\simeq\mathcal O_X$.
nodes.title: Cartier divisors

nodes.statement:
For $n\geq1$, every divisor on $\mathbb P^n$ is linearly equivalent to a unique multiple of a
hyperplane; hence $\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb P^n)\simeq\mathbb Z$ generated by a hyperplane.
nodes.title: Divisors on projective space

nodes.statement:
If $Y$ is a proper closed subset of a noetherian integral scheme $X$, restriction induces an exact
sequence $\operatorname{Div}_Y(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X\setminus Y)\to0$.
nodes.title: Restriction of divisors

nodes.statement:
If $X$ satisfies the standing hypotheses of this section, then $X\times\mathbb A^1$ also satisfies
them, and
\[
\operatorname{Cl}X\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cl}(X\times\mathbb A^1)
\]
via pullback along the projection.
nodes.title: Affine-line invariance of the class group

nodes.statement:
For a complete nonsingular curve, every Weil divisor is Cartier, and the divisor of a nonzero
rational function is the sum of its valuations at the closed points with finite support.
nodes.title: Divisors on nonsingular curves

nodes.statement:
A nonconstant map of complete nonsingular curves is finite. For $Q\in Y$,
$f^*Q=\sum_{f(P)=Q}v_P(t)P$, where $t$ is a uniformizer at $Q$, and this is independent of $t$.
nodes.title: Finite maps of curves

nodes.statement: For a finite map of nonsingular complete curves, $\deg f^*D=(\deg f)\deg D$.
nodes.title: Degree pullback

nodes.statement: A principal divisor on a complete nonsingular curve has degree zero.
nodes.title: Principal divisors have degree zero

nodes.statement:
On an integral separated noetherian normal scheme, Cartier divisors map to Weil divisors by taking
the valuations at codimension-one points, and this map identifies principal Cartier divisors with
principal Weil divisors.
nodes.title: Cartier and Weil divisors

nodes.statement:
For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$, its dual $\mathcal L^{-1}$ is invertible and
$\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}\simeq\mathcal O_X$; isomorphism classes form the Picard group
$\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ under tensor product.
nodes.title: Invertible sheaves and duals

nodes.statement:
The map $D\mapsto\mathcal O_X(D)$ induces an isomorphism from Cartier divisors modulo principal
divisors to $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$.
nodes.title: Cartier divisors and the Picard group

nodes.statement:
On an integral scheme, the map from Cartier divisors modulo principal divisors to the divisor class
group is injective.
nodes.title: Cartier-to-Weil injectivity

nodes.statement:
An effective Cartier divisor is locally defined by a non-zero-divisor. Its ideal sheaf is invertible,
and the quotient defines a closed subscheme of pure codimension one.
nodes.title: Effective Cartier divisors

nodes.statement:
On a locally factorial scheme every Weil divisor is Cartier, and the Cartier and Weil class groups
are canonically isomorphic.
nodes.title: Locally factorial schemes

nodes.statement: For $n\geq1$, $\operatorname{Pic}(\mathbb P^n)\simeq\mathbb Z$, generated by $\mathcal O(1)$.
nodes.title: Class group of projective space

nodes.statement:
Effective Cartier divisors on $X$ are in bijection with closed subschemes whose ideal sheaf is
invertible and locally generated by a non-zero-divisor.
nodes.title: Effective Cartier divisors and closed subschemes

nodes.statement:
A morphism is projective if it factors as a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n_Y$. An
invertible sheaf is relatively very ample when it is the pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ under such an embedding.
nodes.title: Projective morphism

nodes.statement:
A morphisms $f:X\to\mathbb P^n_Y$ is equivalent to an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $X$
together with generating global sections $s_0,\ldots,s_n$, up to the natural change of basis.
nodes.title: Morphisms to projective space

nodes.statement:
A morphism defined by generating sections of an invertible sheaf is a closed immersion precisely
when the induced maps on the standard affine opens identify their coordinate rings with the relevant
affine coordinate rings.
nodes.title: Closed immersion criterion

nodes.statement:
For a finite-type scheme over a field, a finite-dimensional space of sections of an invertible sheaf
defines a closed immersion into projective space iff it separates points and tangent vectors.
nodes.title: Projective embedding criterion

nodes.statement:
If a local homomorphism of noetherian local rings induces a finite extension on residue fields and
the target is generated by finitely many elements over the image, then the corresponding morphism is
finite on a neighborhood.
nodes.title: Finite generation from local maps

nodes.statement:
For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on a noetherian scheme, the following are equivalent: $\mathcal L$
is ample; every coherent sheaf becomes generated by global sections after a positive twist; and a
sufficiently high power of $\mathcal L$ gives a projective embedding on every affine neighborhood.
nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves

nodes.statement: Every projective morphism is proper.
nodes.title: Projective implies proper

nodes.statement:
A nonzero section of an invertible sheaf determines an effective Cartier divisor of zeros. The
complete linear system of an invertible sheaf is the projective space of its nonzero global sections,
and its associated map is the map defined by those sections.
nodes.title: Divisors of zeros and linear systems

nodes.statement:
A linear system has no base points precisely when its sections generate the associated invertible
sheaf; in that case it defines a morphism to projective space.
nodes.title: Base-point-free linear systems

nodes.statement:
For a graded ring $S$, $\operatorname{Proj}S\simeq\operatorname{Proj}S(d)$ after replacing the grading
by a positive twist; the standard opens and their structure sheaves are unchanged.
nodes.title: Proj invariant under twisting

nodes.statement:
If $S$ is a finitely generated graded algebra over $A=S_0$, then $\operatorname{Proj}S\to\operatorname{Spec}A$
is projective.
nodes.title: Relative Proj is projective

nodes.statement:
For a quasi-coherent module $\mathcal E$ on $Y$, $\operatorname{Proj}\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)$
represents invertible quotients of the pullback of $\mathcal E$.
nodes.title: Relative Proj of a symmetric algebra

nodes.statement:
Morphisms $T\to\operatorname{Proj}\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)$ over $Y$ are equivalent to pairs
consisting of an invertible sheaf on $T$ and a surjection from the pullback of $\mathcal E$.
nodes.title: Universal property of relative Proj

nodes.statement:
For the blow-up $\operatorname{Bl}_\mathcal I X=\operatorname{Proj}\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n$,
the inverse image of $\mathcal I$ is an invertible ideal sheaf.
nodes.title: Blow-up ideal

nodes.statement:
The blow-up of $X$ along $\mathcal I$ is universal among morphisms $g:Y\to X$ for which
$g^{-1}\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ is invertible.
nodes.title: Universal property of blow-up

nodes.statement:
If a morphism pulls one ideal sheaf into another, it induces the corresponding morphism of blow-ups;
in particular blow-up commutes with base change in the stated ideal-theoretic sense.
nodes.title: Functoriality of blow-up

nodes.statement: The blow-up of a variety along a coherent ideal is projective over the variety and is again a variety.
nodes.title: Blow-ups of varieties

nodes.statement:
Every projective morphism of noetherian schemes factors as a blow-up followed by a closed immersion
into projective space (after choosing a suitable coherent ideal).
nodes.title: Factorization through a blow-up

nodes.statement:
For $A\to B$, $\Omega_{B/A}$ represents $A$-derivations: it is generated by symbols $db$ with
$d(b+b')=db+db'$, $d(bb')=b\,db'+b'\,db$, and $da=0$.
nodes.title: Kahler differentials

nodes.statement:
Let $B$ be an $A$-algebra, let $I$ be the kernel of the multiplication map
$B\otimes_A B\to B$, and define $db=1\otimes b-b\otimes1$ modulo $I^2$.  Then
$(I/I^2,d)$ is a module of relative differentials for $B/A$.
nodes.title: Diagonal description

nodes.statement:
If $A'$ and $B$ are $A$-algebras and $B'=B\otimes_AA'$, then
$\Omega_{B'/A'}\simeq\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BB'$.  If $S$ is a multiplicative system in $B$, then
$\Omega_{S^{-1}B/A}\simeq S^{-1}\Omega_{B/A}$.
nodes.title: Base change and localization

nodes.statement:
For ring maps $A\to B\to C$ there is a natural exact sequence of $C$-modules
\[
\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BC\longrightarrow\Omega_{C/A}\longrightarrow\Omega_{C/B}\longrightarrow0.
\]
nodes.title: First exact sequence

nodes.statement:
If $B$ is an $A$-algebra, $I\subset B$ an ideal, and $C=B/I$, then there is an exact sequence
\[
I/I^2\xrightarrow{\delta}\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BC\longrightarrow\Omega_{C/A}\longrightarrow0,
\]
where $\delta(\bar b)=db\otimes1$.
nodes.title: Second exact sequence

nodes.statement:
If $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-algebra, or a localization of one, then $\Omega_{B/A}$ is a
finitely generated $B$-module.
nodes.title: Finite generation of differentials

nodes.statement:
For a finitely generated extension field $K/k$, $\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}\ge\operatorname{trdeg}_kK$, with
equality if and only if $K/k$ is separably generated.
nodes.title: Separability criterion

nodes.statement:
Let $B$ be a local ring containing a field $k$ isomorphic to its residue field $B/\mathfrak m$.  Then
$\delta:\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to\Omega_{B/k}\otimes_Bk$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.title: Residue-field differentials

nodes.statement:
Let $B$ be a local ring containing a perfect field $k$ isomorphic to its residue field, and assume
$B$ is a localization of a finitely generated $k$-algebra.  Then $\Omega_{B/k}$ is free of rank
$\dim B$ if and only if $B$ is a regular local ring.
nodes.title: Regularity via differentials

nodes.statement:
If $A$ is a noetherian local integral domain with residue field $k$ and quotient field $K$, and $M$ is
a finite $A$-module satisfying $\dim_k(M\otimes_Ak)=\dim_K(M\otimes_AK)=r$, then $M$ is free of rank $r$.
nodes.title: Free-module criterion

nodes.statement:
For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, the sheaf of relative differentials $\Omega_{X/Y}$ is obtained
on affine opens from the modules $\Omega_{B/A}$ and glued using localization; equivalently, it is
the pullback of the conormal sheaf of the diagonal $X\to X\times_YX$.
nodes.title: Sheaf of relative differentials

nodes.statement:
For $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$, with $X'=X\times_YY'$, one has
$\Omega_{X'/Y'}\simeq g'^*\Omega_{X/Y}$, where $g':X'\to X$ is the projection.
nodes.title: Base change for sheaf differentials

nodes.statement:
For morphisms $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$, there is an exact sequence
\[
f^*\Omega_{Y/Z}\longrightarrow\Omega_{X/Z}\longrightarrow\Omega_{X/Y}\longrightarrow0.
\]
nodes.title: Transitivity sequence

nodes.statement:
If $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed subscheme with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ and $X\to Y$ is a
morphism, then there is an exact sequence on $Z$
\[
\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2\xrightarrow{\delta}\Omega_{X/Y}\otimes\mathcal O_Z\longrightarrow\Omega_{Z/Y}\longrightarrow0.
\]
nodes.title: Closed-subscheme sequence

nodes.statement:
On $\mathbb P^n_A$,
\[
0\to\Omega_{\mathbb P^n_A/A}\to\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus(n+1)}
\xrightarrow{(x_0,\ldots,x_n)}\mathcal O\to0.
\]
nodes.title: Euler sequence

nodes.statement: If $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is a regular local ring, every localization $A_\mathfrak p$ is regular.
nodes.title: Localization of regular local rings

nodes.statement:
For a variety over a perfect field, a point is nonsingular if and only if the stalk of
$\Omega_{X/k}$ is free of rank $\dim X$.
nodes.title: Differential criterion for nonsingularity

nodes.statement: For a variety over a perfect field, the nonsingular locus is open and dense.
nodes.title: Open dense nonsingular locus

nodes.statement:
A finite-type variety $X$ over a perfect field is nonsingular if and only if $\Omega_{X/k}$ is
locally free of rank $\dim X$; for a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow Y$ between nonsingular
varieties, the conormal sequence is exact on the left as well.
nodes.title: Conormal characterization

nodes.statement:
If $X\subset\mathbb P^n$ is nonsingular over an infinite perfect field, a general hyperplane
section of $X$ is nonsingular (or empty).
nodes.title: Bertini for hyperplane sections

nodes.statement: The geometric genus of a nonsingular projective variety is invariant under birational equivalence.
nodes.title: Birational invariance of geometric genus

nodes.statement: $\bigwedge^n\Omega_{\mathbb P^n_A/A}\simeq\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_A}(-n-1)$.
nodes.title: Canonical sheaf of projective space

nodes.statement:
For a noetherian local ring, a quotient of a regular local ring by a regular sequence is
Cohen--Macaulay; equivalently, its depth equals its dimension.
nodes.title: Cohen--Macaulay criteria

nodes.statement:
A noetherian ring is normal if and only if it satisfies $(R_1)$, regularity at codimension-one
primes, and $(S_2)$, depth at least the minimum of $2$ and the local dimension.
nodes.title: Serre normality criterion

nodes.statement:
A local complete intersection in a nonsingular variety is Cohen--Macaulay and is regular in
codimension one.
nodes.title: Local complete intersections

nodes.statement: The blow-up of a nonsingular variety along a local complete intersection is nonsingular.
nodes.title: Blow-up along a local complete intersection

nodes.statement:
If $K/k$ is a separable field extension and $X$ is a nonsingular variety over $k$, then
$X_K=X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ is nonsingular.
nodes.title: Separable scalar extension

nodes.statement:
An adic ring $A$ is complete and separated for the topology defined by an ideal of definition $I$. Its
formal spectrum $\operatorname{Spf}A$ has the open prime ideals containing a power of $I$ and the completed
structure sheaf.
nodes.title: Adic rings and formal spectra

nodes.statement:
For a closed subscheme defined by $\mathcal I$, the formal completion is the ringed space represented
by the compatible thickenings $X_n=(X,\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I^{n+1})$. A coherent formal module is a
compatible inverse system of coherent modules on $X_n$.
nodes.title: Formal completion
Affine formal schemes

nodes.statement:
A morphism into a formal completion is equivalent to a compatible system of morphisms into all
infinitesimal thickenings; coherent formal modules are equivalent to compatible coherent systems
under adic completeness.
nodes.title: Formal functions

nodes.statement:
For a Noetherian ring $A$ and ideal $I$, completion is exact on finitely generated modules, and the
completed module is finite over the completed ring; an already complete module is recovered by completion.
nodes.title: Completed modules

nodes.statement:
If $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Y=V(I)$, the formal completion is
$\operatorname{Spf}\widehat A$ with reductions $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$.
nodes.title: Formal affine schemes

nodes.statement:
Any two ideals of definition on a Noetherian formal scheme give canonically the same formal scheme and
the same category of coherent formal modules.
nodes.title: Independence of ideal of definition

nodes.statement:
A coherent formal module is locally the completion of a finite module, and each reduction modulo a
power of an ideal of definition is coherent.
nodes.title: Coherent formal modules

nodes.statement:
Coherent formal modules are equivalent to compatible systems of coherent modules on all infinitesimal
thickenings.
nodes.title: Formal coherent-module equivalence

nodes.statement: Completion preserves short exact sequences of coherent formal modules.
nodes.title: Exactness of completion

nodes.statement: Kernels, cokernels, and images of morphisms of coherent formal modules are coherent.
nodes.title: Kernels, cokernels, and images

nodes.statement:
There is a unique pairing
\[
 \operatorname{Div}X\times\operatorname{Div}X\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,
 \qquad (C,D)\longmapsto C.D,
\]
such that: (i) if nonsingular curves meet transversally, \(C.D\) is the number
of their intersection points; (ii) \(C.D=D.C\); (iii) it is additive in each
variable; and (iv) it depends only on the linear-equivalence classes of the two
divisors.
nodes.title: Intersection pairing

nodes.statement:
If \(C_1,\ldots,C_r\) are irreducible curves and \(A\) is very ample, a general
member of \(|A|\) is irreducible, nonsingular, and transverse to every \(C_i\).
nodes.title: Bertini choice

nodes.statement:
If \(C\) is nonsingular and \(D\) is transverse to it, then
\[
 C.D=\deg_C\bigl(\mathcal L(D)\otimes\mathcal O_C\bigr).
\]
nodes.title: Intersection with a smooth curve

nodes.statement:
If curves \(C,D\) have no common component, then
\[
 C.D=\sum_{P\in C\cap D}(C.D)_P,qquad
 (C.D)_P=\length_{\mathcal O_{X,P}}\mathcal O_{X,P}/(f,g),
\]
where \(f,g\) are local equations at \(P\).
nodes.title: Local intersection formula

nodes.statement:
For a nonsingular curve \(C\) of genus \(g\) on \(X\),
\[
 2g-2=C.(C+K_X).
\]
nodes.title: Adjunction formula

nodes.statement:
Put \(l(D)=h^0(X,\mathcal L(D))\), \(s(D)=h^1(X,\mathcal L(D))\), and
\(p_a=\chi(\mathcal O_X)-1\).  Then
\[
 l(D)-s(D)+l(K_X-D)=\frac12D.(D-K_X)+1+p_a.
\]
nodes.title: Riemann--Roch for surfaces

nodes.statement:
If \(H\) is ample, there is an integer \(n_0\) such that
\(H^2(X,\mathcal L(D))=0\) whenever \(D.H>n_0\).
nodes.title: Vanishing in large positive degree

nodes.statement:
If \(D.H>0\) and \(D^2>0\), then \(nD\) is linearly equivalent to an effective
divisor for all sufficiently large \(n\).
nodes.title: Effectivity criterion

nodes.statement:
If \(H\) is ample and \(D\not\equiv0\) with \(D.H=0\), then \(D^2<0\).
Equivalently, the intersection form on \(\operatorname{Num}X_\mathbb R\) has
signature \((1,\rho-1)\).
nodes.title: Hodge index theorem

nodes.statement:
A divisor \(D\) on a nonsingular projective surface is ample if and only if
\(D^2>0\) and \(D.C>0\) for every irreducible curve \(C\).
nodes.title: Nakai--Moishezon criterion

nodes.statement:
If \(D.f=n\ge0\), then \(\pi_*\mathcal L(D)\) is locally free of rank \(n+1\),
\(R^1\pi_*\mathcal L(D)=0\), and \(\pi_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_C\).
nodes.title: Direct images on fibers

nodes.statement:
Every ruled surface is \(\mathbb P_C(\mathcal E)\) for a locally free sheaf
\(\mathcal E\) of rank two.  Conversely \(\mathbb P_C(\mathcal E)\) is ruled,
and \(\mathbb P(\mathcal E)\simeq\mathbb P(\mathcal E')\) over \(C\) exactly
when \(\mathcal E'\simeq\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L\) for an invertible sheaf
\(\mathcal L\).
nodes.title: Projective-bundle description

nodes.statement:
For \(X=\mathbb P_C(\mathcal E)\),
\(\operatorname{Pic}X\simeq\mathbb Z[\mathcal O_X(1)]\oplus\pi^*\operatorname{Pic}C\).
After choosing a section \(C_0\), \(\operatorname{Num}X\simeq\mathbb Z C_0\oplus\mathbb Z f\),
with \(C_0.f=1\) and \(f^2=0\).
nodes.title: Picard and numerical groups

nodes.statement:
If \(D.f\ge0\), then \(R^i\pi_*\mathcal L(D)=0\) for \(i>0\), and
\[
 H^i(X,\mathcal L(D))\simeq H^i(C,\pi_*\mathcal L(D)).
\]
nodes.title: Cohomology of nonnegative fiber degree

nodes.statement:
For a ruled surface over a curve of genus \(g\),
\[
 p_a(X)=-g,\qquad p_g(X)=0,\qquad q(X)=g.
\]
nodes.title: Invariants of a ruled surface

nodes.statement:
A section \(D\subset\mathbb P_C(\mathcal E)\) is equivalent to a surjection
\(\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L\) onto an invertible sheaf.  If
\(0\to\mathcal N\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal L\to0\), then
\[
 \mathcal N\simeq\pi_*(\mathcal O_X(1)\otimes\mathcal O_X(-D)),qquad
 \pi_*\mathcal N\simeq\mathcal O_X(1)\otimes\mathcal O_X(-D)
\]
under the natural identification on the base.
nodes.title: Sections and quotient bundles

nodes.statement:
Every locally free sheaf of rank two on a smooth curve is an extension of two
invertible sheaves.
nodes.title: Extensions on curves

nodes.statement:
Every ruled surface has a normalized presentation \(X=\mathbb P(\mathcal E)\),
where \(H^0(\mathcal E)\ne0\) but \(H^0(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal L)=0\) for every
line bundle \(\mathcal L\) of negative degree.  The integer
\(e=-\deg\mathcal E\) is presentation-independent, and there is a section
\(C_0\) with \(\mathcal O_X(C_0)\simeq\mathcal O_X(1)\).
nodes.title: Normalization and the invariant

nodes.statement:
If a section \(D\) corresponds to \(\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L\), then
\[
 \deg\mathcal L=C_0.D,\qquad D\sim C_0+(\deg\mathcal L-e)f,
 \qquad C_0^2=-e.
\]
nodes.title: Classes of sections

nodes.statement:
For the normalized notation, with \(K_C\) also denoting a divisor pulled back
from \(C\),
\[
 K_X\sim -2C_0+(K_C+ef).
\]
nodes.title: Canonical divisor of a ruled surface

nodes.statement:
\[
 K_X\equiv-2C_0+(2g-2-e)f,qquad K_X^2=8(1-g).
\]
nodes.title: Canonical self-intersection

nodes.statement:
For a normalized rank-two bundle on a genus-\(g\) curve, if it is decomposable
then \(\mathcal E\simeq\mathcal O_C\oplus\mathcal L\) with \(\deg\mathcal L\le0\),
so \(e\ge0\), and every \(e\ge0\) occurs.  If it is indecomposable, then
\[
 -2g\le e\le2g-2.
\]
nodes.title: Normalized bundles

nodes.statement:
Over \(C=\mathbb P^1\), every ruled surface is isomorphic to exactly one
\(X_e=\mathbb P(\mathcal O\oplus\mathcal O(-e))\), with \(e\ge0\).
nodes.title: Rational ruled surfaces

nodes.statement:
Every locally free rank-two sheaf on \(\mathbb P^1\) is a direct sum of line
bundles.
nodes.title: Splitting on the projective line

nodes.statement:
For an elliptic curve, an indecomposable normalized rank-two bundle has
\(e=0\) or \(e=-1\), and there is exactly one ruled-surface isomorphism class
for each value.
nodes.title: Indecomposable elliptic ruled surfaces

nodes.statement:
Indecomposable rank-two bundles of each fixed degree on an elliptic curve are
parametrized by the points of the curve (after the natural determinant/twist
identifications).
nodes.title: Atiyah's elliptic classification

nodes.statement:
Let \(X_e=\mathbb P(\mathcal O\oplus\mathcal O(-e))\).  A section
\(D\sim C_0+nf\) exists exactly when \(n=0\) or \(n\ge e\); for \(n=e\) there
is a disjoint section \(C_1\sim C_0+ef\) with \(C_1^2=e\).  Moreover
\(|C_0+nf|\) is base-point-free iff \(n\ge e\), and very ample iff \(n>e\).
nodes.title: Linear systems on \(X_e\)

nodes.statement:
For \(D=aC_0+bf\) on \(X_e\), \(D\) is ample iff it is very ample iff
\(a>0\) and \(b>ae\).  A general member of such a system is irreducible and
nonsingular.
nodes.title: Ample and very ample classes on \(X_e\)

nodes.statement:
For \(n\ge e\), \(|C_0+nf|\) embeds \(X_e\) as a rational scroll of degree
\(2n-e\) in \(\mathbb P^{2n-e+1}\).
nodes.title: Rational scrolls

nodes.statement:
If \(e\ge0\) and an irreducible curve \(Y\) is neither \(C_0\) nor a fiber,
then \(Y\sim aC_0+bf\) with \(a>0\) and \(b\ge ae\).  A divisor
\(D=aC_0+bf\) is ample iff \(a>0\) and \(b>ae\).
nodes.title: Curves and ampleness for \(e\ge0\)

nodes.statement:
Assume \(e<0\) and either characteristic zero or \(g\le1\).  If
\(Y\sim aC_0+bf\) is irreducible and is neither a section nor a fiber, then
\(a>0\) and \(b\ge ae/2\).  A divisor \(D=aC_0+bf\) is ample iff
\(a>0\) and \(b>ae/2\).
nodes.title: Curves and ampleness for \(e<0\)

nodes.statement:
If \(\pi:\widetilde X\to X\) is the blow-up of a nonsingular point \(P\) on a
nonsingular projective surface, then \(\widetilde X\) is nonsingular and
projective, the exceptional curve \(E=\pi^{-1}(P)\) is \(\mathbb P^1\), and
\(E^2=-1\).
nodes.title: The blow-up of a point

nodes.statement:
\[
 \operatorname{Pic}\widetilde X\simeq\pi^*\operatorname{Pic}X\oplus\mathbb Z[E],
 \quad (\pi^*C).(\pi^*D)=C.D,\quad \pi^*C.E=0,\quad E^2=-1,
\]
and \(C.\pi_*D=(\pi^*C).D\).
nodes.title: Picard group and intersections after blowing up

nodes.statement:
\[
 K_{\widetilde X}=\pi^*K_X+E,\qquad K_{\widetilde X}^2=K_X^2-1.
\]
nodes.title: Canonical divisor under a blow-up

nodes.statement:
\[
 \pi_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}=\mathcal O_X,qquad
 R^i\pi_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}=0\ (i>0),
\]
so \(H^i(X,\mathcal O_X)\simeq H^i(\widetilde X,\mathcal O_{\widetilde X})\).
nodes.title: Cohomology under a blow-up

nodes.statement: \(p_a(X)=p_a(\widetilde X)\); in particular \(q\) and \(p_g\) are unchanged.
nodes.title: Arithmetic genus

nodes.statement:
If an effective curve \(C\) has multiplicity \(r\) at \(P\), then
\[
 \pi^*C=\widetilde C+rE.
\]
nodes.title: Total and strict transforms

nodes.statement:
With the notation of Proposition~\ref{ha-v3-6},
\[
 \widetilde C.E=r,qquad p_a(\widetilde C)=p_a(C)-\frac12r(r-1).
\]
nodes.title: Genus drop on blowing up

nodes.statement:
Repeatedly blowing up singular points of an irreducible curve produces, after
finitely many steps, a nonsingular strict transform.
nodes.title: Resolution of an irreducible curve

nodes.statement:
For every curve \(Y\subset X\), a finite sequence of monoidal transformations
makes the total inverse image a divisor with normal crossings: every component
is nonsingular, intersections are transverse, and no two components meet in more
than one local branch.
nodes.title: Embedded resolution of curves

nodes.statement:
Conics through at most four assigned points in \(\mathbb P^2\), with no three
collinear, have no unassigned base points, including an assigned point infinitely
near another.
nodes.title: Conics through assigned points

nodes.statement:
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{ha-v4-1}, the system of conics has
dimension \(5-r\) for \(r\le4\); for five points there is a unique irreducible
conic.
nodes.title: Dimension of conic systems

nodes.statement:
Cubics through at most seven assigned points, with no four collinear and no seven
on a conic, have no unassigned base points, including infinitely near points.
nodes.title: Cubics through assigned points

nodes.statement:
The system of cubics through \(r\le7\) points in the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{ha-v4-3} has dimension \(9-r\).  For \(r=8\), it has dimension
one and its general member is irreducible.
nodes.title: Dimensions of cubic systems

nodes.statement:
Eight points in general position determine a ninth point, possibly infinitely
near, common to every cubic through the eight.
nodes.title: The ninth base point

nodes.statement:
If assigned points satisfy no three collinear and no six on a conic, the cubics
through them induce a very ample linear system on their blow-up.
nodes.title: Very ampleness of cubics on the blow-up

nodes.statement:
Blowing up \(r=0,\ldots,6\) general points of \(\mathbb P^2\) embeds the result
in \(\mathbb P^{9-r}\) with degree \(9-r\), and
\(\omega_{X'}\simeq\mathcal O_{X'}(-1)\).  For \(r=6\), the image is a
nonsingular cubic surface in \(\mathbb P^3\).
nodes.title: Del Pezzo embeddings

nodes.statement:
For \(X=\operatorname{Bl}_{P_1,\ldots,P_6}\mathbb P^2\), let \(l\) be the pullback
of a line and \(e_i\) the exceptional classes.  Then
\[
 l^2=1,\ l.e_i=0,\ e_i.e_j=-\delta_{ij},\quad
 h=3l-\sum e_i,\quad K_X=-h,
\]
and for \(D\sim al-\sum b_ie_i\),
\[
 \deg_hD=3a-\sum b_i,\quad D^2=a^2-\sum b_i^2,quad
 p_a(D)=1+\tfrac12(D^2-\deg_hD).
\]
nodes.title: Picard calculations on a cubic surface

nodes.statement:
The cubic surface contains exactly 27 lines, namely
\[
 e_i\ (1\le i\le6),\qquad l-e_i-e_j\ (i<j),\qquad
 2l-\sum_{j\ne i}e_j\ (1\le i\le6).
\]
They are all the curves of self-intersection \(-1\).
nodes.title: The twenty-seven lines

nodes.statement:
Any six mutually disjoint lines on a cubic surface are the exceptional curves
of a morphism \(X\to\mathbb P^2\); thus they define a second blow-up presentation.
nodes.title: Six skew lines

nodes.statement:
For a divisor \(D\) on a nonsingular cubic surface, the following are equivalent:
\(D\) is very ample; \(D\) is ample; \(D^2>0\) and \(D.L>0\) for every line
\(L\); and \(D.L>0\) for every line \(L\).
nodes.title: Ampleness on a cubic surface

nodes.statement:
If \(D\sim al-\sum b_ie_i\), \(b_1\ge\cdots\ge b_6>0\), and
\(a\ge b_1+b_2+b_5\), then \(D\) is very ample.
nodes.title: A sufficient very-ampleness decomposition

nodes.statement:
For \(D\sim al-\sum b_ie_i\), ampleness and very ampleness are equivalent to
\[
 b_i>0,\qquad a>b_i+b_j\ (i\ne j),\qquad
 2a>\sum_{i\ne j}b_i\quad\text{for every }i.
\]
Every such class contains an irreducible nonsingular member.
nodes.title: Numerical criterion on a cubic surface

nodes.statement:
For a birational map from a normal projective variety, the fundamental locus is
closed and has codimension at least two.
nodes.title: Fundamental points

nodes.statement:
For a birational map of normal projective surfaces, the total transform of each
fundamental point is connected and has dimension at least one.
nodes.title: Zariski's main theorem for a fundamental point

nodes.statement:
If \(f:X'\to X\) is a birational morphism of nonsingular projective surfaces,
and \(P\) is a fundamental point of \(f^{-1}\), then \(f\) factors through the
blow-up \(\pi:\widetilde X\to X\) at \(P\): there is \(f':X'\to\widetilde X\)
with \(f=\pi f'\).
nodes.title: Factorization through a point blow-up

nodes.statement:
If \(n(f)\) is the number of irreducible curves contracted by a birational
morphism \(f:X'\to X\) of nonsingular projective surfaces, then \(f\) is a
composition of exactly \(n(f)\) monoidal transformations.
nodes.title: Birational morphisms

nodes.statement:
Every birational transformation between nonsingular projective surfaces is a
composition of monoidal transformations and their inverses.
nodes.title: Factorization of birational transformations

nodes.statement:
The arithmetic genus of a nonsingular projective surface is a birational
invariant.
nodes.title: Birational invariance of surface arithmetic genus

nodes.statement:
If \(Y\simeq\mathbb P^1\) on a nonsingular projective surface and \(Y^2=-1\),
there is a morphism contracting \(Y\) to a nonsingular point, and this morphism
is inverse to the blow-up of that point.
nodes.title: Castelnuovo contraction

nodes.statement:
Every nonsingular projective surface admits a birational morphism to a relatively
minimal surface, i.e. one with no exceptional curve of the first kind.
nodes.title: Relatively minimal models

nodes.statement:
\[
 \kappa(X)=-1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |12K_X|=\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X\text{ is rational or ruled}.
\]
nodes.title: The case \(\kappa=-1\)

nodes.statement:
For a nonsingular projective surface, \(X\) is rational if and only if
\(p_a(X)=0\) and \(P_2=0\), where
\(P_2=h^0(X,\mathcal O_X(2K_X))\).
nodes.title: Castelnuovo rationality criterion

nodes.statement:
If \(\operatorname{char}k\ne2,3\), then
\(\kappa(X)=0\) iff \(|12K_X|\) consists of one divisor (equivalently
\(P_{12}=1\)).  The minimal surfaces with \(\kappa=0\) are K3 surfaces,
Enriques surfaces, abelian surfaces, and hyperelliptic (bielliptic) surfaces,
distinguished by their canonical torsion and invariants \(p_g,q\).
nodes.title: The case \(\kappa=0\)

nodes.statement:
\(\kappa(X)=1\) if and only if \(X\) is an elliptic surface: after a birational
modification it admits a fibration to a curve whose general fiber is a smooth
curve of genus one.
nodes.title: The case \(\kappa=1\)

nodes.statement:
\(\kappa(X)=2\) if and only if some pluricanonical system \(|nK_X|\) defines a
birational map onto its image.  Such surfaces are precisely the surfaces of
general type.
nodes.title: The case \(\kappa=2\)

nodes.statement: For smooth projective $X/k$ of dimension $n$, $Z(X,t)$ is rational.
nodes.title: Weil rationality

nodes.statement:
If $E$ is the self-intersection number of a hyperplane section of $X$, then
$Z(1/(q^nt))=\pm q^{nE/2}t^E Z(t)$.
nodes.title: Weil functional equation

nodes.statement:
There are integer polynomials $P_i(t)$, with $P_0(t)=1-t$ and
$P_{2n}(t)=1-q^nt$, such that
$Z(t)=P_1(t)P_3(t)\cdots P_{2n-1}(t)/(P_0(t)P_2(t)\cdots P_{2n}(t))$,
and every reciprocal root of $P_i$ is an algebraic integer of absolute value
$q^{i/2}$.
nodes.title: Weil weights

nodes.statement:
Assuming C.1.3, $B_i=\deg P_i$ are the Betti numbers and
$E=\sum_i(-1)^iB_i$; these agree with the topological Betti numbers when
$X$ is lifted to characteristic zero.
nodes.title: Betti numbers

nodes.statement:
$H^i(X,\mathbb Q_\ell)$ is finite-dimensional and vanishes for $i<0$ and
$i>2n$ when $\dim X=n$.
nodes.title: Finite-dimensionality

nodes.statement: $H^i(-,\mathbb Q_\ell)$ is contravariant in $X$.
nodes.title: Contravariance

nodes.statement:
There is a cup product
$H^i(X,\mathbb Q_\ell)\otimes H^j(X,\mathbb Q_\ell)\to H^{i+j}(X,\mathbb Q_\ell)$.
nodes.title: Cup product

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is smooth proper of dimension $n$, $H^{2n}(X,\mathbb Q_\ell)$ is
one-dimensional and cup product gives a perfect pairing
$H^i(X)\times H^{2n-i}(X)\to H^{2n}(X)$.
nodes.title: Poincare duality

nodes.statement:
If $f:X\to X$ has isolated multiplicity-one fixed points, then
$L(f,X)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(f^*;H^i(X,\mathbb Q_\ell))$.
nodes.title: Lefschetz fixed point formula

nodes.statement:
For a smooth proper morphism with connected base, $\dim H^i(X_y,\mathbb Q_\ell)$
is constant; in particular it is invariant under finite-field extension.
nodes.title: Smooth proper base change

nodes.statement:
For smooth proper $X/\CC$,
$H^i(X,\mathbb Q_\ell)\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\CC\simeq H^i(X_h,\CC)$.
nodes.title: Comparison over the complex numbers
Cycle classes

nodes.statement:
For an endomorphism $\varphi$ of a finite-dimensional vector space $V$,
\[
\exp\left(\sum_{r\ge1}\operatorname{Tr}(\varphi^r;V)\frac{t^r}{r}\right)
=\det(1-t\varphi;V)^{-1}.
\]
nodes.title: Determinant identity

nodes.statement:
Put $P_i(t)=\det(1-tF^*;H^i(X,\mathbb Q_\ell))$.  Then
\[
Z(X,t)=\prod_{i=0}^{2n}P_i(t)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
\]
Consequently $Z(X,t)$ is rational.  Moreover $P_0(t)=1-t$ and
$P_{2n}(t)=1-q^nt$.
nodes.title: Cohomological zeta formula

nodes.statement:
If $V\times W\to K$ is a perfect pairing and endomorphisms $\varphi,\psi$
satisfy $\langle\varphi v,\psi w\rangle=\lambda\langle v,w\rangle$,
then
\[
\det(1-t\psi;W)=(-1)^rt^r\lambda^r
\frac{\det(1-(\lambda t)^{-1}\varphi;V)}{\det(\varphi;V)}.
\]
nodes.title: Perfect-pairing determinant identity

nodes.statement:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem 4.2,
\[
Z(1/(q^nt))=\pm q^{nE/2}t^E Z(t),
\qquad E=\sum_i(-1)^i\dim H^i(X,\mathbb Q_\ell).
\]
nodes.title: Functional equation

nodes.statement:
The reciprocal roots of each $P_i(t)$ are algebraic integers $\alpha_{ij}$
with $|\alpha_{ij}|=q^{i/2}$.  Hence the Weil conjectures all hold.
nodes.title: Deligne's theorem

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is projective over $\CC$, analytification gives an equivalence between
coherent algebraic sheaves on $X$ and coherent analytic sheaves on $X_h$;
for every coherent $\mathcal F$ the comparison maps
\[
\alpha_i:H^i(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(X_h,\mathcal F_h)
\]
are isomorphisms.
nodes.title: GAGA

nodes.statement:
Every compact analytic subspace of $\mathbb P^n_h$ is the analytification of
a unique closed algebraic subscheme of $\mathbb P^n$.
nodes.title: Chow

nodes.statement: Every compact complex manifold of dimension one is projective algebraic.
nodes.title: Riemann

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is a normal scheme of finite type over $\CC$, and $X'$ is a normal
complex analytic space with a finite morphism $f:X'\to X_h$, then there is a
unique normal scheme $X'$ and finite morphism $g:X'\to X$ such that
$X'_h\simeq X'$ and $g_h=f$.  Consequently
\[
\pi_1^{\mathrm{alg}}(X)\simeq\widehat{\pi_1(X_h)}.
\]
nodes.title: Generalized Riemann existence

nodes.statement:
For a compact complex manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, the meromorphic function
field has transcendence degree at most $n$ over $\CC$; if equality holds, it is
a finitely generated extension of $\CC$.  If $X=X_h$ is algebraic, then this
field is the algebraic rational function field.
nodes.title: Siegel

nodes.statement:
Every compact complex manifold of dimension two with two algebraically
independent meromorphic functions is projective algebraic.
nodes.title: Chow--Kodaira

nodes.statement: Every Hodge manifold is projective algebraic.
nodes.title: Kodaira

nodes.statement: Every Moishezon manifold which is Kähler is projective algebraic.
nodes.title: Moishezon

    (by
      intro A hA
      change IsAlgebraicSet k n (⋂₀ A)
      have hAi : ∀ a : A, IsAlgebraicSet k n (a : Set (AffinePoint k n)) :=

theorem hilbertNullstellensatz [IsAlgClosed k]
    (I : Ideal (AffinePolynomial k n)) (f : AffinePolynomial k n)
    (hf : ∀ P ∈ commonZeroSet k n (I : Set (AffinePolynomial k n)),
      evaluate k n f P = 0) :
    ∃ r : ℕ, 0 < r ∧ f ^ r ∈ I := by
  have hfvan : f ∈ vanishingIdeal k n
      (commonZeroSet k n (I : Set (AffinePolynomial k n))) := hf
  rw [vanishingIdeal_commonZeroSet_eq_radical] at hfvan
  rcases (Ideal.mem_radical_iff.mp hfvan) with ⟨m, hm⟩
  refine ⟨m + 1, Nat.zero_lt_succ m, ?_⟩
  simpa [pow_succ] using I.mul_mem_right f hm

variable (k : Type*) [Field k] (n : Nat)

theorem vanishingIdeal_isPrime_of_isAffineVariety
    {Y : Set (AffinePoint k n)} (hY : IsAffineVariety k n Y) :
    (vanishingIdeal k n Y).IsPrime := by
  rw [Ideal.isPrime_iff]
  constructor
  · intro htop
    rcases hY.nonempty with ⟨P, hP⟩
    have hone : (1 : AffinePolynomial k n) ∈ vanishingIdeal k n Y := by
      rw [htop]
      exact Submodule.mem_top
    have hzero := hone P hP
    simp [evaluate] at hzero
  · intro f g hfg
    have hcover : Y ⊆ zeroSet k n f ∪ zeroSet k n g := by
      have hcover0 : Y ⊆ zeroSet k n (f * g) := by
        intro P hP
        change evaluate k n (f * g) P = 0
        exact hfg P hP
      rw [zeroSet_mul] at hcover0
      exact hcover0
    have hsplit :
        Y ⊆ zeroSet k n f ∨ Y ⊆ zeroSet k n g :=
      (isPreirreducible_iff_isClosed_union_isClosed.mp hY.isIrreducible.isPreirreducible
        (zeroSet k n f) (zeroSet k n g)
        (isClosed_zeroSet k n f) (isClosed_zeroSet k n g) hcover)
    rcases hsplit with hf | hg
    · left
      intro P hP
      exact hf hP
    · right
      intro P hP
      exact hg hP

def affineRadicalIdealToAlgebraicSet :
    AffineRadicalIdeal k n → AffineAlgebraicSet k n := by
  intro I
  exact ⟨commonZeroSet k n (I : Ideal (AffinePolynomial k n)),
    ⟨(I : Ideal (AffinePolynomial k n)), rfl⟩⟩

theorem affineRadicalIdealToAlgebraicSet_leftInverse
    (Y : AffineAlgebraicSet k n) :
    affineRadicalIdealToAlgebraicSet k n
        (affineAlgebraicSetToRadicalIdeal k n Y) = Y := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  exact commonZeroSet_vanishingIdeal_eq_self k n Y.property

theorem affineAlgebraicSetToRadicalIdeal_antitone
    {Y Z : AffineAlgebraicSet k n}
    (hYZ : (Y : Set (AffinePoint k n)) ⊆ Z) :
    affineAlgebraicSetToRadicalIdeal k n Z ≤
      affineAlgebraicSetToRadicalIdeal k n Y := by
  exact vanishingIdeal_mono k n hYZ

  {I : Ideal (AffinePolynomial k n) // I.IsRadical}

  {Y : Set (AffinePoint k n) // IsAlgebraicSet k n Y}

def affineNullstellensatzEquiv :
    AffineAlgebraicSet k n ≃ AffineRadicalIdeal k n where
  toFun := affineAlgebraicSetToRadicalIdeal k n
  invFun := affineRadicalIdealToAlgebraicSet k n
  left_inv := affineRadicalIdealToAlgebraicSet_leftInverse k n
  right_inv := affineAlgebraicSetToRadicalIdeal_rightInverse k n

theorem vanishingIdeal_radical_of_isAffineVariety
    {Y : Set (AffinePoint k n)} (hY : IsAffineVariety k n Y) :
    (vanishingIdeal k n Y).radical = vanishingIdeal k n Y :=
  (vanishingIdeal_isPrime_of_isAffineVariety k n hY).radical

Algebraic sets correspond inclusion-reversingly to radical ideals by $Y\mapsto I(Y)$ and
$\mathfrak a\mapsto Z(\mathfrak a)$.  An algebraic set is irreducible exactly when its ideal is prime.
nodes.title: Affine Nullstellensatz correspondence

@[simp]
nodes.statement: For an affine algebraic set $Y$, put $A(Y)=A/I(Y)$.
nodes.title: Affine coordinate ring

nodes.statement:
In a noetherian topological space, every nonempty closed set is a finite union of irreducible
closed subsets, uniquely after omitting components contained in another.
nodes.title: Irreducible components

nodes.statement: Every affine algebraic set is a unique irredundant union of affine varieties.
nodes.title: Affine components

nodes.statement: For an affine algebraic set $Y$, $\dim Y=\dim A(Y)$.
nodes.title: Dimension of an affine coordinate ring

nodes.statement:
If $B$ is a finitely generated domain over a field $k$, then
$\dim B=\operatorname{trdeg}_kK(B)$ and
$\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p+\dim(B/\mathfrak p)=\dim B$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$.
nodes.title: Dimension theorem for finite type domains

nodes.statement: \(\dim\mathbb A^n=n\).
nodes.title: Dimension of affine space

nodes.statement: If $Y$ is quasi-affine, then $\dim Y=\dim\overline Y$.
nodes.title: Dimension of a quasi-affine variety

nodes.statement:
If $A$ is noetherian and $f$ is neither a zero divisor nor a unit, every minimal prime containing
$f$ has height one.
nodes.title: Krull Hauptidealsatz

nodes.statement: A noetherian domain is a unique factorization domain iff every height-one prime is principal.
nodes.title: Height-one criterion for a UFD

nodes.statement:
A variety $Y\subset\mathbb A^n$ has dimension $n-1$ iff $Y=Z(f)$ for one nonconstant irreducible
$f\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$.
nodes.title: Affine hypersurfaces

nodes.statement:
The projective space $\mathbb P^n$ is the set of nonzero $(n+1)$-tuples in $k^{n+1}$ modulo
scalar multiplication. A homogeneous polynomial has all terms of one total degree, and $S$ is
graded by total degree.
nodes.title: Projective space and homogeneous coordinates

nodes.statement:
For homogeneous $T\subset S$, define $Z(T)\subset\mathbb P^n$ by common vanishing. A projective
algebraic set is a set $Z(T)$; its homogeneous vanishing ideal is $I(Y)$ and its homogeneous
coordinate ring is $S(Y)=S/I(Y)$.
nodes.title: Projective algebraic set

nodes.statement:
A projective variety is an irreducible projective algebraic set. A quasi-projective variety is an
open subset of a projective variety.
nodes.title: Projective and quasi-projective varieties

nodes.statement:
Unions and arbitrary intersections of projective algebraic sets are algebraic, as are $\varnothing$
and $\mathbb P^n$.
nodes.title: Projective algebraic sets

nodes.statement:
With $H_i=Z(x_i)$ and $U_i=\mathbb P^n-H_i$, the ratio map
$\varphi_i:U_i\to\mathbb A^n$ is a homeomorphism for the induced/projective and affine Zariski
topologies.
nodes.title: Standard projective charts

nodes.statement:
Every projective (respectively quasi-projective) variety is covered by its intersections with the
$U_i$, which are affine (respectively quasi-affine) varieties.
nodes.title: Affine chart cover

nodes.statement:
A function to $k$ is regular at $P$ if on a neighborhood of $P$ it is $g/h$ with $h$ nowhere
zero; in projective space $g,h$ are homogeneous of the same degree. It is regular if it is regular
at every point.
nodes.title: Regular function

nodes.statement:
A morphism is a continuous map pulling regular functions back to regular functions. An isomorphism
is a morphism having a morphism as inverse.
nodes.title: Morphism and isomorphism

nodes.statement: Every regular function is continuous.
nodes.title: Continuity of regular functions

nodes.statement:
For affine $Y$, $\mathcal O(Y)\cong A(Y)$; points correspond to maximal ideals; for $P$,
$\mathcal O_{P,Y}\cong A(Y)_{\mathfrak m_P}$ and $\dim\mathcal O_{P,Y}=\dim Y$; and
$K(Y)$ is the fraction field of $A(Y)$ with transcendence degree $\dim Y$.
nodes.title: Affine variety functions and local rings

nodes.statement: The chart map $\varphi_i:U_i\to\mathbb A^n$ of Proposition 2.2 is an isomorphism of varieties.
nodes.title: Projective chart isomorphism

nodes.statement:
For projective $Y$ with homogeneous coordinate ring $S(Y)$, $\mathcal O(Y)=k$,
$\mathcal O_{P,Y}=S(Y)_{(\mathfrak m_P)}$, and $K(Y)$ is the degree-zero fraction field
$S(Y)_{((0))}$.
nodes.title: Functions on a projective variety

nodes.statement:
For any variety $X$ and affine variety $Y$, morphisms $X\to Y$ correspond naturally to
$k$-algebra homomorphisms $A(Y)\to\mathcal O(X)$.
nodes.title: Maps to affine varieties

nodes.statement:
A map $\psi:X\to Y\subset\mathbb A^n$ is a morphism iff every coordinate function $x_i\circ\psi$
is regular on $X$.
nodes.title: Coordinate criterion for affine morphisms

nodes.statement: Affine varieties are isomorphic iff their coordinate rings are isomorphic as $k$-algebras.
nodes.title: Affine anti-equivalence

nodes.statement:
$X\mapsto A(X)$ is an arrow-reversing equivalence between affine varieties over $k$ and finitely
generated integral $k$-domains.
nodes.title: Affine varieties and finite type domains

nodes.statement:
If $A$ is a finitely generated domain over $k$, $L$ is finite algebraic over $K(A)$, and $A'$ is
the integral closure of $A$ in $L$, then $A'$ is a finite $A$-module and a finitely generated
$k$-algebra.
nodes.title: Finiteness of integral closure

nodes.statement:
A rational map $X\dashrightarrow Y$ is an equivalence class of morphisms from nonempty open
subsets of $X$, where two representatives agree after restriction to a common nonempty open.
It is dominant if its image is dense, and birational if it has an inverse rational map.
nodes.title: Rational and birational maps

nodes.statement:
For an irreducible variety $X$, its function field $K(X)$ is the field of rational functions,
equivalently the fraction field of the coordinate ring of any dense affine open subset.
nodes.title: Function field

nodes.statement: Two morphisms from $X$ to $Y$ agreeing on a nonempty open subset agree everywhere.
nodes.title: Density determines morphisms

nodes.statement:
If $Y=V(f)\subset\mathbb A^n$, then $\mathbb A^n-Y$ is isomorphic to
$H=V(x_{n+1}f-1)\subset\mathbb A^{n+1}$, and its coordinate ring is $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_f$.
nodes.title: Principal open as affine

nodes.statement: Every variety has a basis of open affine subsets.
nodes.title: Affine basis

nodes.statement:
Dominant rational maps $X\dashrightarrow Y$ correspond bijectively to $k$-embeddings
$K(Y)\hookrightarrow K(X)$, giving an arrow-reversing equivalence with finitely generated field
extensions of $k$.
nodes.title: Rational maps and function fields

nodes.statement:
For varieties $X,Y$, the following are equivalent: $X,Y$ are birational; they have isomorphic
dense open subsets; and $K(X)\cong K(Y)$ over $k$.
nodes.title: Birational tests

nodes.statement:
A finite separable extension $L/K$ is generated by one element; over an infinite $K$, a generator
can be chosen as a $K$-linear combination of any finite generating set.
nodes.title: Primitive element

nodes.statement:
Every finitely generated separably generated extension has, inside any generating set, a separating
transcendence basis.
nodes.title: Separating transcendence bases

nodes.statement: Every finitely generated extension of a perfect field is separably generated.
nodes.title: Perfect fields

nodes.statement:
Every $r$-dimensional variety is birational to a hypersurface in $\mathbb A^{r+1}$ (and to its
projective closure in $\mathbb P^{r+1}$).
nodes.title: Birational hypersurface model

nodes.statement:
For a point $P$ of an affine variety, let $\mathfrak m_P$ be the maximal ideal of its local ring.
The cotangent space is $\mathfrak m_P/\mathfrak m_P^2$ and the Zariski tangent space is its dual.
nodes.title: Local, cotangent, and tangent spaces

nodes.statement:
A noetherian local ring $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ is regular if
$\dim_k\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2=\dim A$. A variety is nonsingular at $P$ when its local ring is
regular, and singular otherwise.
nodes.title: Regular local ring and nonsingularity

nodes.statement:
The multiplicity of a local ring is the normalized leading coefficient of its Hilbert--Samuel
polynomial; at a point of a variety it is the multiplicity of its local ring.
nodes.title: Multiplicity

nodes.statement:
For an affine variety $Y\subset\mathbb A^n$, $P$ is nonsingular iff $\mathcal O_{P,Y}$ is
regular.  If $\dim Y=r$, this is equivalent to the Jacobian of generators of $I(Y)$ having rank
$n-r$ at $P$.
nodes.title: Jacobian criterion

nodes.statement: For a noetherian local ring $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$, \(\dim_k\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\ge\dim A\), with equality precisely when $A$ is regular.
nodes.title: Embedding-dimension inequality

nodes.statement: For every variety $Y$, $\operatorname{Sing}Y$ is a proper closed subset.
nodes.title: Openness of the nonsingular locus

nodes.statement:
For a noetherian local ring $A$ with completion $\widehat A$: $\widehat A$ is local with maximal
ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ and $A\hookrightarrow\widehat A$; the completion of every finite
$A$-module $M$ is $M\otimes_A\widehat A$; \(\dim\widehat A=\dim A\); and $A$ is regular iff
$\widehat A$ is regular.
nodes.title: Completion of local rings

nodes.statement:
If a complete regular local ring of dimension $n$ contains a field, then it is isomorphic to
$k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ over its residue field $k$.
nodes.title: Cohen structure theorem

nodes.statement:
For homogeneous polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ with indeterminate coefficients, there are universal
integer-coefficient polynomials in those coefficients, homogeneous in the coefficients of each
$f_i$, whose simultaneous vanishing is equivalent over every field to the existence of a common
nonzero projective zero.
nodes.title: Elimination theory

nodes.statement:
A curve is a one-dimensional variety. A valuation ring of a field $K$ is a local subring $R$
such that for every $x\in K^*$ either $x$ or $x^{-1}$ lies in $R$. It is discrete when its value
group is $\mathbb Z$, in which case it is a discrete valuation ring (DVR).
nodes.title: Curves, valuation rings, and DVRs

nodes.statement:
A local ring $R$ dominates a local ring $A$ when $A\subseteq R$ and the maximal ideal of $R$
contracts to that of $A$. An abstract nonsingular curve is the curve obtained by gluing the local
models associated to the DVRs of its function field.
nodes.title: Domination and abstract nonsingular curve

nodes.statement:
A local subring $R\subset K$ is a valuation ring iff for each $x\in K^*$, $x\in R$ or
$x^{-1}\in R$.
nodes.title: Valuation rings

nodes.statement: A one-dimensional noetherian local domain is a DVR iff it is integrally closed.
nodes.title: One-dimensional normal local rings

nodes.statement: The integral closure of a Dedekind domain in a finite extension of its fraction field is Dedekind.
nodes.title: Integral closure of a Dedekind domain

nodes.statement:
If $P\ne Q$ are points of a quasi-projective variety with the same function field, neither local
ring dominates the other.
nodes.title: Incomparability of curve local rings

nodes.statement:
For a one-dimensional function field $K/k$ and $x\in K^*$, $x$ belongs to a valuation ring $R$
iff it has nonnegative valuation there; if $x\notin R$, then $x^{-1}$ lies in the maximal ideal.
The intersection of the valuation rings containing $k$ is the relative constant field.
nodes.title: Valuation-ring intersection

nodes.statement:
Every DVR of a one-dimensional function field $K/k$ is isomorphic to the local ring of a point on
a nonsingular affine curve.
nodes.title: DVRs are curve local rings

nodes.statement:
Every nonsingular quasi-projective curve is isomorphic to an abstract nonsingular curve formed from
the DVRs of its function field.
nodes.title: Abstract model of a nonsingular curve

nodes.statement:
A morphism from an open subset of a nonsingular curve to a nonsingular complete curve extends
uniquely across the finitely many omitted points.
nodes.title: Extension across finitely many points

nodes.statement:
Every one-dimensional function field $K/k$ has a nonsingular projective curve $C_K$ whose points
are exactly the DVRs of $K/k$; it is unique up to unique isomorphism.
nodes.title: Complete nonsingular model

nodes.statement:
Every abstract nonsingular curve is quasi-projective, and every nonsingular quasi-projective curve is
an open subset of a nonsingular projective curve.
nodes.title: Projective completion of curves

nodes.statement: Every curve is birationally equivalent to a nonsingular projective curve.
nodes.title: Nonsingular projective model

nodes.statement:
The categories of nonsingular projective curves with dominant morphisms, quasi-projective curves
with dominant rational maps, and one-dimensional function fields over $k$ with $k$-homomorphisms
are equivalent.
nodes.title: Equivalent categories of curves

nodes.statement:
If $Y,Z\subset\mathbb A^n$ have dimensions $r,s$, every irreducible component of $Y\cap Z$ has
dimension at least $r+s-n$.
nodes.title: Affine dimension theorem

nodes.statement:
For varieties $Y,Z\subset\mathbb P^n$ of dimensions $r,s$, every component of $Y\cap Z$ has
dimension at least $r+s-n$; if $r+s-n\ge0$, then $Y\cap Z\ne\varnothing$.
nodes.title: Projective dimension theorem

nodes.statement:
A numerical polynomial is a polynomial taking integer values at all sufficiently large integers.
For a finite graded module, its Hilbert polynomial is the numerical polynomial agreeing eventually
with the Hilbert function.
nodes.title: Numerical and Hilbert polynomials

nodes.statement:
(a) Every numerical polynomial has a unique integer expansion \(P(z)=\sum_{i=0}^r c_i\binom zi\).
(b) If a function $f:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$ has eventually numerical-polynomial first difference,
then $f$ agrees eventually with a numerical polynomial.
nodes.title: Numerical polynomials

nodes.statement:
Every finite graded module over a noetherian graded ring has a finite graded filtration whose factors
are shifts of $S/\mathfrak p_i$ for homogeneous primes.  Every prime containing $\operatorname{Ann}M$
contains some $\mathfrak p_i$; the minimal such primes are the minimal primes of $M$, and each occurs
with multiplicity equal to $\length_{S_\mathfrak p}M_\mathfrak p$.
nodes.title: Graded-module filtration

nodes.statement:
For a finite graded module $M$ over $S=k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$, the Hilbert function agrees for all
large integers with a unique polynomial $P_M(z)$, and \(\deg P_M=\dim Z(\operatorname{Ann}M)\).
nodes.title: Hilbert--Serre

nodes.statement:
The degree of a projective variety is the leading coefficient of its Hilbert polynomial multiplied
by the factorial of its dimension.
nodes.title: Degree
Degree

nodes.statement:
The intersection multiplicity of a component in a hypersurface intersection is the length of the
corresponding localized graded module.
nodes.title: Intersection multiplicity

nodes.statement:
Let $Y\subset\mathbb P^n$ have dimension at least one and let $H$ be a hypersurface not containing
$Y$.  If $Z_1,\ldots,Z_s$ are the components of $Y\cap H$, and
$i(Y,H;Z_j)$ is the multiplicity of the corresponding minimal prime, then
\[
\sum_j i(Y,H;Z_j)\deg Z_j=(\deg Y)(\deg H).
\]
nodes.title: Intersection with a hypersurface

nodes.statement:
Distinct plane curves of degrees $d,e$ with finite intersection points $P_1,\ldots,P_s$ satisfy
$\sum_i i(Y,Z;P_i)=de$.
nodes.title: Bezout
